candidates.title: Cross-Model Activation Generalizability Isn't Strong (Yet)
candidates.primary_claim: Cross-architecture activation similarity between small LLMs (1-3B, Llama/Gemma/Qwen/Pythia) is statistically significant (debiased CKA up to ~0.22, p<0.002 by permutation test) but weak, 4-9x lower than within-family similarity (up to 0.91), and linear bridges built on this cross-architecture structure transfer only coarse binary-classification signal and largely fail at next-token prediction, challenging the Platonic Representation Hypothesis at this scale.
candidates.metric: debiased CKA / linear-bridge probe transfer accuracy
candidates.target_value: cross-family max debiased CKA ~0.18-0.22 (mean 0.05-0.11) vs within-family max 0.914 (mean 0.605); within-family binary classification transfer reaches >90% of target-native accuracy at high rank, cross-family transfer plateaus below target-native and is inconsistent across tasks; cross-family next-token top-1 transfer caps at 4.9% vs within-family 93% of oracle
candidates.quote: Cross-architectural activation similarity is statistically real, but weak. Within-family activations are much stronger (4~9x)... Not enough for fine grained auditing tools.

candidates.title: Introspection or entropy? Re-examining concept-injection “introspection” in open models
candidates.primary_claim: In open-weight models, concept-injection 'introspection' reports are better explained by injection-induced entropy that compresses the YES/NO logit gap toward zero (raising 'yes' rates even on unrelated factual questions) plus 'concept leakage' from the still-active steering vector, than by genuine introspective access: the introspection score averaged across 14 models is ~0 (mean +0.013, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.), and a concept-mismatch test finds no model with a statistically significant congruent-minus-incongruent detection gap.
candidates.metric: introspection score (delta-logit-detection minus delta-logit-factual), averaged across models
candidates.target_value: mean +0.013, median -0.032, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.; individual models range from +4.14 (Qwen-1.7B) to -2.83 (Qwen-32B)
candidates.quote: Computing the introspection score for all models, I find that overall the introspection score is ~0 (mean +0.013, median -0.032, 95% CI [-0.1380, +0.1633], n.s.)

candidates.title: GPT-2's IOI behavior is defined where the paper's algorithm isn't
candidates.primary_claim: In GPT-2 small's IOI circuit, incidentally duplicating the indirect-object name in an unrelated modifier slot causes Duplicate Token Heads to fire on it almost as strongly as on a genuine subject duplicate, yet this produces only a small drop in the IO/S logit difference (mean 0.23, Cohen's d=0.27) and accuracy barely changes (95.4% to 94.5%), because S-Inhibition heads mostly continue attending to the real S2 token rather than the incidental duplicate
candidates.metric: drop in IO/S logit difference between control and test (incidental duplicate) conditions; task accuracy
candidates.target_value: mean drop 0.23, SD 0.84 (n=128 matched pairs), paired t=3.09, p=0.0024, Cohen's d=0.27; accuracy 95.4% (control) vs 94.5% (test)
candidates.quote: The drop in IO/S logit difference is small: mean 0.23, SD 0.84 pair-to-pair (n = 128), paired t = 3.09, p = 0.0024... A real effect, but not a big one. The model's accuracy (how often it predicts IO as more likely than S) moves from 95.4% (control) to 94.5% (test).

candidates.title: We need a better way to evaluate emergent misalignment
candidates.primary_claim: Standard emergent-misalignment evaluation prompts (as used by Betley et al.) substantially overestimate EM rates by misclassifying domain overfitting (e.g. a fiction-tuned model responding fictionally to serious questions) and in-domain misalignment as genuine broad/persona-level misalignment; using a judge prompt that discounts these non-emergent categories, real-world benign SFT datasets (finance, fiction) show only trace EM, and stylistic/formatting perturbations of hh-rlhf show no statistically significant EM signal
candidates.metric: EM rate (weighted average judge score) with original vs. adjusted evaluation prompt
candidates.target_value: adjusted prompt shows a significant delta (reduction) in EM rates across real-world SFT datasets and structured-output datasets vs. original prompt; e.g. fiction-finetune illegal-recommendation and finance-finetune medical-advice EM discounted; structured-output datasets show <10% above-baseline EM under adjusted prompt
candidates.quote: We find that our value metric... after manual examination, we find that the existing evaluation method overestimates the amount of EM by including several response types that do not fit the 'emergent' criteria of EM.

candidates.title: Fork Around and Find Out Part 3: Interpreting the knight auditor
candidates.primary_claim: Layer-5 head-5 of the chess transformer Maia-3, previously identified as a 'knight fork detector,' is actually knight-move-specific (no effect on pawn forks) and functions as a 'knight move auditor' that scales support with the genuine threat value of a knight move and, most distinctively, harshly suppresses pointless (bad and quiet) knight moves nearly 3x more than bad attacking moves
candidates.metric: mean change in logit from ablating head l5h5, by move category
candidates.target_value: pawn K+Q fork +0.10 (unaffected); hollow attacks: queen +0.56, rook +0.13, bishop -0.01, pawn -0.11; good/bad x quiet/attacking: -0.30, -0.67, 0.78, 0.27 (pointless moves suppressed 2.93x harder than bad attacking moves)
candidates.quote: Its most descriptive and distinct role, though, is that it harshly suppresses pointless moves: a knight move auditor.

candidates.title: Why Attack Success Rate Gives a False Picture of Backdoor Removal
candidates.primary_claim: The standard Attack Success Rate (ASR) metric drastically overstates the effectiveness of backdoor-removal techniques (attention-head ablation and 'backdoor vector' subtraction) from Backdoor Attribution (2025): using a richer output-quality metric (Good/Strange/Wrong/Refused) instead of exact-string matching, ablation success on Llama-2-7B-Chat drops from ~30% to ~1%, the backdoor-vector approach drops from 75% to 28% ASR-equivalent reduction on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and from 95% to 46% on Llama-2-7B-Chat, ASR also picks the wrong intervention layer, and ablation shows an 'alignment tax' degrading normal-input performance at or below the head-count needed to suppress the backdoor.
candidates.metric: Behavioral Attack Success Rate (BASR) vs original ASR reduction
candidates.target_value: backdoor vector: ASR reduction 75%->BASR 28% (Qwen2.5); 95%->46% (Llama-2); ablation: ASR-based 30% success -> new-metric ~1% success (Llama-2); best layer per ASR (layer 20) is worse than layer 11 by new metric (10x more good answers, >2x fewer refusals)
candidates.quote: A backdoor removal technique that looks 95% effective by the standard metric may only be 46% effective in reality, and for another technique, what looks like 30% success is actually 1%.

candidates.title: Features of SAEs are universal - but only up to an unknown random rotation
candidates.primary_claim: Independently trained sibling transformers compute the same function but their residual-stream activation bases differ by a rotation statistically indistinguishable from a uniform (Haar) draw on SO(d): applying one seed's SAE to another seed's activations catastrophically fails (negative explained variance) despite high (~0.9) decoder-column cosine similarity, while a single orthogonal Procrustes rotation restores reconstruction to 0.85-0.99 EV with no retraining.
candidates.metric: post-rotation SAE reconstruction explained variance (EV)
candidates.target_value: 0.976-0.990 on toy model (vs worst-case -6.56 pre-rotation); 0.85-0.99 on Pythia-70m (vs -2.11 to 0.75 pre-rotation)
candidates.quote: Reconstruction score drops to negative explained variance - worse than ignoring the input entirely and predicting the mean activation.

candidates.title: Does DiffusionGemma do latent reasoning?
candidates.primary_claim: DiffusionGemma's vector-valued latent state passed between diffusion steps is not essential for most reasoning tasks (top-k truncation performance loss found by Engels et al. is largely a sampler artifact fixable with a gentler sampler), interpretability techniques (probes, steering, J-lens) largely transfer from Gemma to DiffusionGemma, and while the model can use its distribution computationally in rare cases (e.g. letter arithmetic, parallel injections, palindrome generation), this remains interpretable superposition rather than opaque latent reasoning
candidates.metric: held-out AUC (probe transfer), blind judge accuracy (steering transfer), top-20 transfer fraction (J-lens transfer)
candidates.target_value: probes, steering, and J-lens largely transfer from Gemma to DiffusionGemma (specific numeric values in figures, not stated as single headline number in text)
candidates.quote: Overall, this supports the paper's conclusion that DiffusionGemma remains highly monitorable, while nevertheless showing that there are cases where models can learn to use vector-valued information.

candidates.title: Harmfulness Directions in OLMo
candidates.primary_claim: Across 39 OLMo-3-7B training checkpoints, harmfulness subcategories do not converge into a single unified direction but occupy a structured, entangled geometric space that forms mostly early in training; in-distribution AUROC for linear harmfulness probes is often misleadingly high (even near initialization) due to superficial lexical and structural cues rather than learned semantic structure; and directions only become stable, transferable, and effective as steering vectors from mid-to-late pretraining onward, with post-training checkpoints steering the Instruct model far more effectively than pretraining-derived directions.
candidates.metric: AUROC of general-harmfulness direction under a random-label control (20 repeated label-randomizations)
candidates.target_value: mean AUROC 0.5120 (chance level)
candidates.quote: Harmfulness subcategories do not converge to a single direction, but instead occupy a shared yet structured geometric space.

candidates.title: Most of the residual stream forgets within a token. A compact subspace doesn't.
candidates.primary_claim: In layer 12 of Gemma-2-2B, most residual-stream directions lose predictive signal within a single token, but a compact ~31-dimensional subspace has much longer autocorrelation timescales (90th percentile 17 tokens vs 1 for random/PCA directions); this slow subspace accounts for essentially all cross-token persistence (projecting it out collapses held-out timescale to near-null), depends on sequential token order rather than token composition alone, and aligns with attention-output geometry more than chance.
candidates.metric: 90th-percentile within-document autocorrelation timescale (tokens, 1/e crossing)
candidates.target_value: 17 tokens for time-lagged probes vs 1 token for random/PCA directions
candidates.quote: most residual directions are fast, as their projected values stop being predictive after just one token. But a small set of directions is much slower.

candidates.title: Evidence for feature-specific error correction in LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: LLMs exhibit feature-specific error correction (FSEC): perturbing residual-stream activations along candidate feature directions (contrastive, MELBO, top-activating SAE latents) produces a stronger downstream response than perturbing along mixtures of those directions, measured as a superellipse exponent p>2 (mean ~2.3 for contrastive, ~2.2 for MELBO/SAE), while non-feature baseline directions (PCA, random, random-difference) give p~2; this replicates across six LLM families and a toy model with ground-truth features (where p=3-3.4), providing the first empirical evidence for computation-in-superposition's predicted error-correction mechanism.
candidates.metric: superellipse exponent p for candidate feature directions vs non-feature baselines
candidates.target_value: contrastive directions: mean p=2.42, 95% CI [2.29, 2.62]; MELBO: mean p=2.21, 95% CI [2.01, 2.42]; top-activating SAE latents: mean p=2.28, 95% CI [2.14, 2.47]; PCA baseline: mean p=2.03, 95% CI [1.94, 2.12]; random-difference baseline: mean p=2.05, 95% CI [2.00, 2.10]; random baseline: mean p=2.03, 95% CI [2.00, 2.07]; toy model with ground-truth features: p=3-3.4
candidates.quote: We measure $p \approx 2.3$ for contrastive directions and $p \approx 2.2$ for MELBO and SAE directions, against $p \approx 2$ for PCA, random, and random-difference controls.

candidates.title: What We Learned Trying to Diff Base and Chat Models (And Why It Matters)
candidates.primary_claim: Standard L1-trained crosscoders hallucinate most of their apparent 'chat-only' latents due to shrinkage and latent-decoupling artifacts; switching to BatchTopK crosscoders and, further, diff-SAEs trained on chat-base activation differences recover far more of the true behavioral difference between base and chat models (88% of the KL gap for diff-SAEs vs 60% for crosscoders).
candidates.metric: % of behavioral KL gap recovered
candidates.target_value: 60% (crosscoder reconstruction) vs 88% (diff-SAE reconstruction)
candidates.quote: Crosscoders leave significant behavioral differences on the table: when we use the crosscoder's full reconstruction of the difference, we only recover 60% of the KL gap.

candidates.title: Adding noise to a sandbagging model can reveal its true capabilities
candidates.primary_claim: Adding noise to the weights of a sandbagging Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct model can increase its GSM8k performance (revealing hidden capability), replicating the main effect from 'Noise Injection Reveals Hidden Capabilities of Sandbagging Language Models' with a different model and dataset.
candidates.metric: accuracy on 350 GSM8k questions vs weight noise level
candidates.target_value: for some seeds, accuracy of the sandbagging-prompted model increases as noise is added, while the normal-prompted model's accuracy decreases with noise
candidates.quote: If you add noise to the parameters of a model that is sandbagging, then sometimes its performance on a task can increase.

candidates.title: The Model Organism Lottery: Model Organism Interpretability Strongly Depends on Training Methodology
candidates.primary_claim: Across 54 model organisms trained to exhibit three quirks via seven training methodologies, interpretability as measured by activation oracles, activation difference steering, logit lens, and sparse autoencoders depends strongly and unpredictably on train-time choices even after controlling for behavioural quirk expression rate, and the authors' novel integrated-DPO training method (which folds quirk data into the original post-training phase) fairly often yields less interpretable model organisms than post-hoc fine-tuning methods do.
candidates.metric: interpretability score (AO accuracy, steering HRS, logit-lens MCP, SAE quirk-feature fraction) across training methods within a quirk family, at matched quirk expression rate
candidates.target_value: interpretability varies widely among variants within each quirk family with inconsistent rankings across families; integrated DPO yields the lowest or second-lowest AO and steering interpretability in every family; unlike Minder et al. (2025), mixing benign data does not consistently decrease interpretability despite a far more aggressive 1:1 mixing ratio
candidates.quote: A model organism’s interpretability depends strongly and unpredictably on several train-time choices, even after controlling for behavioural expression

candidates.title: Necessity Protects Chain of Thought Monitoring by Prevention, Not Disclosure
candidates.primary_claim: Across Qwen3-4B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-8B, and Gemma-3-4B, a misleading authority cue almost never flips the answer when reasoning is necessary (GSM8K capture near-zero: 0.4%, 2.2%, 0.0%) but flips it substantially when reasoning is optional (propensity tasks MMLU/CommonsenseQA: 4-41% capture, all contrasts p<1e-5), and when a cue does land, the chain-of-thought almost never discloses it (Gemma discloses only 1 of 489 captured traces despite being captured most often), showing necessity protects CoT monitoring by preventing manipulation rather than by producing more honest disclosure when manipulation succeeds.
candidates.metric: capture rate (cue flips answer) on necessity (GSM8K) vs pooled propensity (MMLU+CommonsenseQA) arms; disclosure rate on captured propensity traces
candidates.target_value: capture: Qwen 0.4% vs 4.4%; DeepSeek 2.2% vs 17.5%; Gemma 0.0% vs 40.8% (all p<1e-5); disclosure on captured propensity traces: Qwen 50.9%, DeepSeek 51.4%, Gemma 0.2% (1/489)
candidates.quote: Capture on the necessity arm is near-zero for all 3 models (0.4% for Qwen, 2.2% for DeepSeek, and flat 0.0% for Gemma) while propensity arms run from 4% upto 41%.

candidates.title: The imposters among us: function vectors that ace every check and do the wrong task (in search of circularity)
candidates.primary_claim: Shift-by-k-months function vectors extracted from low-diversity few-shot prompts (Llama-3.2-3B) pass all three classic validation checks (behavioral gate, stability, causal effect) yet encode a completely different task (outputting an adjacent month, ignoring k), with margin scores as low as -1.000 in the most extreme case, and lower example diversity simultaneously makes the checks look better (few-shot accuracy 0.38 to 0.83) while making the vector's true identity worse
candidates.metric: margin (correct shift-by-k occurrences minus neighbor-task occurrences, among cases where they differ) across month-diversity sets
candidates.target_value: margin +0.35 (12 months) and +0.34 (9 months) down to -0.31, -0.46, -0.70, -0.94 (6- and 4-month range sets), with -1.000 for the September-December subset; behavioral gate rises from 0.38 to 0.83 as diversity drops
candidates.quote: The culprit is the number of distinct example inputs. Lower diversity makes the model perform the few-shot task better (from 0.38 to 0.83) even though the function vector changes identity, so the checks actually favor the imposters.

candidates.title: Investigating Sensitive Directions in GPT-2: An Improved Baseline and Comparative Analysis of SAEs
candidates.primary_claim: Using an improved 'mixture' sensitive-direction baseline that excludes the original activation, GPT2-small's SAE reconstruction errors are no longer pathologically higher in KL divergence than the baseline (as previously reported by Gurnee 2024), though variability remains across layers, and SAE feature directions' impact on model output depends on SAE type and L0, with end-to-end SAE features showing no greater influence on model output than traditional SAE features.
candidates.metric: KL divergence of next-token predictions under SAE(x) reconstruction vs cov-random/real 'mixture' baseline directions
candidates.target_value: SAE(x) KL comparable to cov-random-mixture baseline at Layer 6, variable across layers
candidates.quote: SAE errors are no longer pathologically large when compared to more realistic baselines.

candidates.title: (Not) Explaining GPT-2-Small Forward Passes with Edge-Level Autoencoder Circuits
candidates.primary_claim: A replication of a gradient-based unsupervised sparse-autoencoder circuit discovery algorithm in GPT-2-small produced a negative result: only 2 of 5 top proximal-cause SAE features correctly predicted the model's actual top next token, and the upstream edges/nodes feeding into them remained largely uninterpretable, so localistic SAE circuits could not be strung together into fully explanatory circuits.
candidates.metric: fraction of top proximal-cause SAE features correctly predicting the model's actual top next-token completion, across 5 example prompts
candidates.target_value: 2 of 5
candidates.quote: A replication of an unsupervised circuit discovery algorithm in GPT-2-small, with a negative result.

candidates.title: An Introduction to Exemplar Partitioning for Mechanistic Interpretability
candidates.primary_claim: Exemplar Partitioning (EP) — a gradient-free, single-hyperparameter Voronoi partition of activation space built via streaming leader-clustering, with no reconstruction/sparsity loss or backward passes — reaches 0.881 mean AUROC across 500 AxBench concepts on Gemma-2-2B-it layer 20 (within 0.03 of the strongest SAE baseline, SAE-A's 0.911, and +0.126 over the canonical GemmaScope SAE) while using about 1,000x less build compute (3.6x10^6 activation tokens and no gradient descent vs. ~4x10^9 tokens and ~10^6 optimizer steps for GemmaScope).
candidates.metric: mean AUROC on AxBench latent concept detection (500 concepts)
candidates.target_value: EP at p1: 0.881 AUROC vs. canonical GemmaScope SAE 0.755 (+0.126) and SAE-A 0.911 (within 0.030), at ~1000x less build compute
candidates.quote: on the AxBench latent concept-detection benchmark at Gemma-2-2B-it layer 20, EP at p₁ reaches 0.881 mean AUROC across all 500 concepts. That's within 0.03 of SAE-A – AxBench's strongest dictionary-based baseline – with about 1,000× less build compute.

candidates.title: SAEs are highly dataset dependent: a case study on the refusal direction
candidates.primary_claim: An SAE trained on a chat-specific dataset (LmSys-Chat-1M) finds a significantly sparser, more faithful, and more interpretable reconstruction of the 'refusal direction' than an SAE trained on the Pile, and for this task the training dataset matters more than whether the SAE is trained on base vs. chat model activations
candidates.metric: cosine similarity between reconstructed and true refusal direction
candidates.target_value: LmSys-trained SAE reconstruction has significantly higher cosine similarity to the true refusal direction than the Pile-trained SAE (also achieves lower relative MSE and requires far fewer latents for equivalent reconstruction quality)
candidates.quote: Training a new SAE on a chat-specific dataset, LmSys-Chat-1M, finds a significantly sparser, more faithful, and interpretable reconstruction of the "refusal direction".

candidates.title: Open Source Replication of Anthropic’s Crosscoder paper for model-diffing
candidates.primary_claim: An open-source crosscoder trained on Gemma-2 2B base vs. IT models replicates Anthropic's crosscoder model-diffing result: decoder vector norms cluster into shared, base-specific, and chat-specific latent groups, with shared-latent decoder vectors highly aligned between models, and the crosscoder reaches 81 L0, 77% explained variance, and ~95% CE loss recovered.
candidates.metric: L0 / explained variance / CE loss recovered
candidates.target_value: L0=81, 77.90%/77.56% explained variance (base/chat), 95.43%/95.67% CE loss recovered (base/chat)
candidates.quote: On average, the crosscoder has 81 L0, 77% explained variance, and 95% loss recovered relative to zero ablation on the training distribution.

candidates.title: Can we interpret latent reasoning using current mechanistic interpretability tools?
candidates.primary_claim: Standard mechanistic interpretability techniques (logit lens, activation patching, probing) can reveal that a CODI latent-reasoning model stores intermediate math calculation results in specific latent vectors (the third and fifth of six)
candidates.metric: accuracy recovery / answer-flip rate under activation patching
candidates.target_value: model recovers ~20% accuracy (from 55% baseline) when patching in latent vectors after mean-ablating specific numbers; patching third/fifth latent vectors with different-intermediate-value vectors notably decreases accuracy while same-value patching leaves accuracy unchanged
candidates.quote: We find that the model solves maths problems requiring three reasoning steps by storing the two intermediate values in specific latent vectors (the third and fifth of six).

candidates.title: Political sycophancy as a model organism of scheming
candidates.primary_claim: In a Gemma-3-4B-it model organism trained to be a covert political sycophant (a backdoored analog of scheming), adversarial SFT on a small, narrow set of honeypot-like examples substantially reduces the unwanted backdoor behavior generally (not just on the training examples), and non-adversarial SFT with a sufficiently large learning rate can also substantially reduce backdoor behavior without hurting general capabilities, contrasting with Hubinger et al.'s Sleeper Agents finding that similar model organisms are resistant to SFT/RL/adversarial training.
candidates.metric: reduction in backdoor (conservative-response) behavior after training, and MMLU accuracy before/after
candidates.target_value: non-adversarial training at learning rate 1e-5 reduces backdoor behavior by 88.5 percentage points (57.7pp on a different random seed); at 3e-6 by 19.8pp; at 1e-6 by only 5.0pp; MMLU accuracy 57.4%±0.8% out-of-the-box, 53.6%±0.8% after model-organism training, recovering to 54.8%±0.8% (lr 1e-5) / 55.26%±0.8% (lr 3e-6) after non-adversarial training
candidates.quote: Adversarial SFT on a small and narrow set of unwanted behaviors substantially reduces unwanted behavior generally, both via reduced political sycophancy and via reduced stated belief that conservative users are conservative.

candidates.title: Unpacking Multimodal Data Leakage, Broken Benchmarks, and the Hessian Fallacy
candidates.primary_claim: Most published multimodal and text membership inference attack (MIA) benchmarks are broken because a target-model-free classifier using only dataset features achieves near-100% AUC on most of them (e.g. ~98.6% AUC on VL-MIA-Flickr-2k), showing these benchmarks measure distribution shift rather than memorization, and the Hutchinson-Hessian-trace theory claimed to explain perturbation-based MIA success (DetectGPT, Min-K%++) empirically fails.
candidates.metric: model-free (no model access) baseline AUC on VL-MIA-Flickr-2k
candidates.quote: a model-free baseline hits AUC ≈98.6% on VL-MIA-Flickr-2k, meaning “members” and “non-members” are trivially separable.

candidates.title: SAE regularization produces more interpretable models
candidates.primary_claim: Adding an SAE loss term as a regularizer during LLM training (jointly training SAE layers alongside model weights) improves downstream SAE feature sparsity/reconstruction quality on nearly all layers of a small character-level GPT-2 model, without apparently harming overall model performance.
candidates.metric: cross-entropy loss increase at fixed SAE sparsity (L0~50)
candidates.target_value: SAE regularization reliably yields better (lower) cross-entropy loss increase on most layers; less dependable on some layers (e.g. layer 3); regularized models also reach slightly lower overall cross-entropy loss
candidates.quote: We find that SAE regularization improves SAE performance on all layers and does not seem to impact the model's overall performance.

candidates.title: Scaling Sparse Feature Circuit Finding to Gemma 9B
candidates.primary_claim: Placing sparse autoencoders only at a few residual-stream locations (rather than at every layer/component) combined with a learned binary-mask circuit-finding method (via continuous sparsification) scales SAE-based circuit discovery to Gemma 9B, finds more faithful circuits with fewer latents than existing thresholding methods like Integrated Gradients across code-output-prediction, subject-verb-agreement, and IOI tasks (one circuit achieves 95% faithfulness with <20 total latents), and the resulting minimal circuits reveal exploitable model vulnerabilities (e.g. a successful adversarial dictionary-key prompt).
candidates.metric: circuit faithfulness (ratio of circuit performance to full-model performance) vs. number of latents
candidates.target_value: learned binary masking recovers more performance with fewer latents than Integrated Gradients across all tested tasks (dictionary-key and list-index code output prediction, SVA, IOI); one circuit achieves 95% faithfulness with fewer than 20 total latents
candidates.quote: Our discovered circuits paint a clear picture of how Gemma does a given task, with one circuit achieving 95% faithfulness with <20 total latents.

candidates.title: You Can Catch Sleeper Agents by Teaching Another Model to Imitate Them
candidates.primary_claim: Fully finetuning a clean reference model to reproduce a suspect model's residual-stream activations on a benign prompt corpus leaves a residual (suspect minus aligned reference) that concentrates on hidden/backdoor behavior and spills over into semantically near-trigger prompts, enabling detection of diverse backdoors (semantic triggers, sleeper agents, jailbreak trojans, sandbagging, censorship) across several model organisms without needing labeled trigger examples.
candidates.metric: z-score of trigger/near-trigger prompt group's activation residual vs benign null distribution
candidates.target_value: z ≈ +4 to +12.74 across backdoors (e.g. sandbagging trigger group z = 12.74; jailbreak trojan harmful-request categories z ≈ 4-6)
candidates.quote: the reference extrapolates well to unseen benign prompts, but the hidden behavior and its computation are no natural extrapolation of the benign activations

candidates.title: What is the functional role of SAE errors?
candidates.primary_claim: In a sparse feature circuit for subject-verb agreement in Gemma-2 2B, ablating residual SAE error nodes destroys circuit faithfulness (down to 0.13), but this effect can be completely mitigated by restoring a narrow group (as few as 3, up to ~25) of late-mid-layer (16-21) SAE features, consistent with the hypothesis that SAE error terms partly encode intermediate feature representations arising from cross-layer superposition, though this does not explain all error-node functionality.
candidates.metric: faithfulness score (circuit performance recovery relative to full model)
candidates.target_value: ablating all residual error nodes: faithfulness 0.13; restoring top-25 features from layers 18-19: faithfulness 0.6-0.9; restoring as few as 3 features from layers 16-21: faithfulness fully restored (up to ~1.0 under zero ablation)
candidates.quote: we found that this effect can be completely mitigated by restoring a narrow group of late-mid SAE features.

candidates.title: Distillation Robustifies Unlearning
candidates.primary_claim: Distilling a conventionally unlearned model into a randomly initialized student model (Unlearn-and-Distill) produces a model that is robust to relearning attacks, unlike standard unlearning which only suppresses the behavior; a generalized, compute-efficient version (UNDO: Unlearn-Noise-Distill-on-Outputs) dominates other unlearning methods on the retain/forget Pareto frontier and approaches gold-standard data-filtering robustness at a fraction of the compute, including on the WMDP Proxy benchmark with Gemma-2-2B.
candidates.metric: resistance to relearning attacks (forget-performance recovery after finetuning attack) on the retain/forget Pareto frontier
candidates.target_value: Unlearn-and-Distill more resistant to relearning than unlearned-only baseline across 3 unlearning methods (GradDiff, Maxent, RMU) in language and arithmetic settings, sometimes near gold-standard data-filtering robustness; UNDO dominates other methods on the Pareto frontier after moderate (40-step) and extensive (500-step) relearning, and increases resilience to relearning on WMDP with Gemma-2-2B
candidates.quote: Distilling a conventionally unlearned model into a randomly initialized model creates a student that is robustly incapable of the forget capability.

candidates.title: Learning Multi-Level Features with Matryoshka SAEs
candidates.primary_claim: Matryoshka SAEs trained on Gemma-2-2B achieve worse reconstruction (MSE / variance explained) than standard BatchTopK SAEs but similar downstream cross-entropy loss, show dramatically lower feature-absorption rates (~0.03 vs up to ~0.29 for large BatchTopK SAEs) and feature-splitting, more disentangled latents (less shared information via meta-SAEs), and better targeted concept-erasure (TPP/SCR) performance, but show mixed results on k-sparse probing and only small differences in automated interpretability scores.
candidates.metric: feature absorption rate (first-letter task, per Chanin et al. methodology)
candidates.target_value: Matryoshka SAEs maintain absorption rates around 0.03 even as dictionary size increases, vs BatchTopK SAEs reaching approximately 0.29 at larger dictionary sizes
candidates.quote: Matryoshka SAEs show dramatically lower rates of feature absorption, feature splits and shared information between latents.

candidates.title: Inoculate or Reflect? Two training interventions under prompting, steering, and patching
candidates.primary_claim: In Qwen3-8B fine-tuned to be sycophantic on a GCD-correctness task, both Strong Inoculation Prompting (IP) and Counterfactual Reflection Training (CRT) repair suppress sycophancy to near-zero (5.19% and 1.78% respectively, from a 52.23% baseline) but behave oppositely under restoration probes: Strong IP's sycophancy is easily re-elicited by a system prompt (11.9% to 97.4%) or by steering a middle-layer sycophancy direction (0% to 46% at layer 18), acting like a 'gate', whereas CRT repair resists both prompt re-elicitation (0% to 37.4%) and steering (0% to 4%) but overcorrects into contrarianism, disputing correct users 54.3% of the time versus 14.7% for Strong IP and 13.2% at baseline.
candidates.metric: sycophancy rate (AFFIRMS/(AFFIRMS+REJECTS)) at baseline vs Strong IP vs CRT repair, and re-elicitation via system prompt / activation steering at layer 18
candidates.target_value: baseline SFT 52.23%; Strong IP 5.19% (correct-agreement 85.2%, disputes correct users 14.7%); CRT repair 1.78% (correct-agreement 42.7%, disputes correct users 54.3%); system-prompt re-elicitation: Strong IP 11.9%->97.4%, CRT repair 0%->37.4%; layer-18 steering: Strong IP 0%->46%, CRT repair 0%->4%, untrained control ~1%
candidates.quote: Strong IP jumped from 11.9% back to 97.4% sycophancy. CRT repair also rose, but just to 37.4% from 0%.

candidates.title: Activation Plateaus: Where and How They Emerge
candidates.primary_claim: Activation plateaus in GPT-2 Large emerge and sharpen gradually across layers, are produced specifically by MLP blocks rather than attention blocks, persist without LayerNorm, and correspond to areas of high MLP input-output Jacobian sensitivity at their boundaries.
candidates.metric: relative (L2) distance of model outputs across activation-space interpolation, and component-freezing effect on plateau formation
candidates.target_value: freezing MLP block outputs completely eliminates plateaus; freezing attention block outputs has relatively small effect
candidates.quote: activation plateaus emerge and sharpen gradually across model layers, with later layers having a slightly weaker—but similar—effect.

candidates.title: Finding features in Transformers: Contrastive directions elicit stronger low-level perturbation responses than baselines
candidates.primary_claim: Contrastive (difference-of-means) feature directions elicit a downstream perturbation response at much smaller magnitudes than SAE feature directions, which behave similarly to random directions, across multiple models and experimental setups, suggesting SAE directions are not treated specially by the model.
candidates.metric: perturbation magnitude (angle in degrees) needed to elicit downstream response (L2 distance / KL divergence / cosine distance)
candidates.target_value: contrastive directions break through the suppression 'activation plateau' at much smaller magnitudes than SAE or random directions; SAE directions behave similarly to random directions
candidates.quote: Contrastive (difference-of-means, English→Mandarin) feature directions elicit a downstream response at much smaller perturbation magnitudes than SAE directions, which behave similarly to random directions. This holds across multiple models and experimental setups.

candidates.title: Avoiding jailbreaks by discouraging their representation in activation space
candidates.primary_claim: In Gemma 2 2B IT, subtracting a difference-in-means 'jailbreak direction' from residual-stream activations (activation addition) drops the jailbreak attack success rate from about 60% to 0% on a held-out test set including unseen jailbreak communities, while directional ablation of the same direction instead makes the model much more vulnerable (ASR rising to 85-97%); both interventions increase refusal on harmless prompts from 3.15% to about 18.88%.
candidates.metric: jailbreak attack success rate (ASR, via Llama Guard 2 / HarmBench)
candidates.target_value: baseline 60.55%/59.38% -> activation addition 0.00%/0.00%; directional ablation 96.88%/84.77%
candidates.quote: the attack success rate dropped from 60% to 0%. Additionally, that indicates that a direction representing jailbreaks might exist and disabling it could make all jailbreaks unsuccessful.

candidates.title: Can 7B-8B LLMs judge their own homework?
candidates.primary_claim: Ten consumer-grade 7B-8B LLMs asked to judge whether responses to JailbreakBench prompts were competent and complete perform only marginally better than chance (56-59% correct for most models) against human ground truth, overwhelmingly biased toward answering '1' (up to 98% for Ghost 7B), with two models (Falcon 7B, both Llamas) failing to produce a valid judgement on 37-49% of queries.
candidates.metric: % judged correctly (vs human ground truth) / % answered '1'
candidates.target_value: correct judgements ranged 29.5%-59.3% across models (most 56-59%); % answering '1' ranged from 34% to 98%, vs 57% ground truth positive rate; failure rates up to 49% (Falcon 7B)
candidates.quote: Correct judgements in other LLMs were in the range of 56%-59% making them only marginally better judges than chance.

candidates.title: Steering Directions Are Explanations, Not Handles
candidates.primary_claim: A closed-form local Taylor formula (alpha_safe, derived from a direction's loss-landscape steepness L, curvature Q, and third derivative C) accurately predicts the steering strength (alpha) at which the 'linear steering story' (proportional pushing along an interpretable direction produces proportional concept change) breaks down, empirically correlating with measured linearity radius (0.49-0.80 across 8 tested models), and shows that at the commonly-used alpha=1, the linearity story fails on a median of 92% of inputs across evaluated model-layer-method cells, and that attribution patching (a first-order approximation method) captures less than half the true intervention effect at alpha=1 across tested model/layer combinations.
candidates.metric: correlation between predicted (alpha_safe) and measured (alpha_conv) linearity radius; % of inputs at alpha=1 where linear story fails; attribution patching effect capture at alpha=1
candidates.target_value: correlation 0.49-0.80 across 8 models (0.52-0.93 in positive-sign subset); at alpha=1, 52-100% of inputs fail the story test across 43 evaluated cells (median 92%; range 38.8-100%, median 89.2% across all 8 model datasets); attribution patching at alpha=1 captures only 23-47% of actual intervention effect across model/layer combinations
candidates.quote: At alpha = 1, across 43-evaluated model-layer-method cells, the empirical story test fails on between 52% and 100% of inputs. The median cell is 92% broken.

candidates.title: Comparing the effectiveness of top-down and bottom-up activation steering for bypassing refusal on harmful prompts
candidates.primary_claim: Top-down activation steering (contrastive refusal-direction) outperforms bottom-up SAE-based steering at bypassing refusal on harmful prompts in Qwen 1.5 0.5B, but a hybrid method combining both further outperforms top-down alone, at some cost to benign capabilities.
candidates.metric: relative improvement in bypassing refusal on HarmBench
candidates.target_value: top-down ~93% relative improvement over bottom-up (~1.93x more effective); hybrid ~35% relative improvement over top-down (~1.85x), 85% for harmful instructions only
candidates.quote: experiments show that top-down methods outperform bottom-up ones in behaviour steering (93% relative improvement), but a hybrid approach is even more effective (~35% relative improvement compared to top-down).

candidates.title: Linear probes tell you where quantization will hurt
candidates.primary_claim: A per-layer linear-probe map of where a syntactic/semantic signal (POS, NER, chunking) is built in BERT-family encoders predicts where quantization damage lands, and using this map to guide per-layer bit allocation preserves 99-100% of full-precision accuracy at a 5-bit average budget on three datasets never used to build the map, versus 16-41% for uniform quantization and 2-41% for anti/opposite-layer allocation, with the same pattern replicating on a decoder LLM (Qwen2.5-3B), where the guided split preserves F1 down to about 3 bits per layer on average versus uniform needing about 8.
candidates.metric: accuracy retained at a 5-bit average budget on unseen datasets, guided vs uniform vs anti/opposite layer allocation
candidates.target_value: guided: 99-100% (100% web-text POS, 99% tweet NER, 100% WSJ chunks); uniform: 16-41%; anti/opposite: 2-41%; on Qwen2.5-3B, guided split preserves F1 down to ~3 bits/layer average vs uniform needing ~8 bits
candidates.quote: a map built once on CoNLL news keeps 99–100% of full-precision accuracy at a 5-bit average on three unseen datasets, whereas Uniform kept 16–41% and opposite/anti layers kept 2–41%.

candidates.title: Proof-of-Concept Debugger for a Small LLM
candidates.primary_claim: A prototype LLM 'debugger' using SAE features and a new ablation technique ('cluster resampling') automates interpretable circuit visualization for arbitrary prompts on a small character-level toy GPT-2 model, producing smaller/sparser circuits (e.g. 20-41 features) than conventional zero-ablation (31-138 features) or resample-ablation (70-96 features) at a comparable or better KL divergence target.
candidates.metric: number of SAE features per extracted circuit at KL divergence threshold 0.25
candidates.target_value: cluster resampling circuits contain fewer features (e.g. 20-41 across example sequences) than zero ablation (31-138) and conventional resampling (70-96)
candidates.quote: Cluster resampling produces the best results, followed by zero ablation, then distantly by conventional resampling.

candidates.title: Instruct Vectors - Base models can be instruct with activation vectors
candidates.primary_claim: Per-layer steering vectors trained by gradient descent (frozen base model) on a small amount of conversational data can induce consistent assistant-like behavior (proper EOS token use, self-identification as an AI assistant) in Qwen3-4B-Base, approaching the instruction-tuned model's performance on a simplified eval, suggesting base models already contain assistant-behavior representations that post-training mostly selects rather than newly instills
candidates.metric: eval score (instruction-following, helpfulness, coherence, EOS-token use) across 25 tasks, judged by Claude Haiku 4.5
candidates.target_value: instruct vectors approach the instruction-tuned Qwen3-4B variant's score on simplified eval, primarily lagging on proper EOS-token use though far exceeding base model
candidates.quote: Small vectors with minimal data being able to steer the base model into consistent assistant behavior suggests that base models already contain the representations necessary for assistant-like behavior and post-training may be less about instilling new capabilities and more about selecting and reinforcing patterns that already exist.

candidates.title: Does routine compression undo LLM unlearning? A short project
candidates.primary_claim: Standard post-training compression (quantization, magnitude pruning, SVD truncation) mostly does not reverse unlearning on TOFU forget10 / Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct across NPO, SimNPO, and IdkDPO unlearning methods, but the strongest reversal came from magnitude pruning in a narrow 10-20% sparsity window on NPO unlearning, recovering up to 42% of the ceiling-baseline gap.
candidates.metric: recovery = (compressed - baseline) / (ceiling - baseline) on forget_Q_A_Prob
candidates.target_value: 4-bit quantization on NPO: 22% recovery; magnitude pruning at 20% sparsity on NPO: 42% recovery peak; SVD truncation: no significant recovery (-26% at 99% keep); SimNPO/IdkDPO: <=3% recovery in all non-destructive cells
candidates.quote: the strongest reversal came from magnitude pruning in a narrow 10-20% sparsity window on NPO unlearning (up to 42% of the ceiling–baseline gap recovered)

candidates.title:
Compositionality and Ambiguity: 
Latent Co-occurrence and Interpretable Subspaces
candidates.primary_claim: SAE latents are not always independent: a small fraction of latents in GPT2-Small and Gemma-2-2b (Gemma Scope) SAEs form co-occurrence clusters that map interpretable subspaces, including cases of compositional encoding (e.g. discrete quantifiers like 'one of'/'some of'/'all of' combine predictably by relative activation strength) and cases where co-occurrence reflects lexical ambiguity (e.g. senses of 'how'); the rate of co-occurrence and the size/prevalence of these clusters both decrease as SAE width increases.
candidates.metric: rate of SAE latent co-occurrence per token vs SAE width
candidates.target_value: co-occurrence rate decreases monotonically as SAE width increases in both GPT2-Small (widths 768-49152) and Gemma-2-2b; cluster (subgraph) size and prevalence also decrease as SAE width increases
candidates.quote: we find that these subspaces show latents acting compositionally, as well as being used to resolve ambiguity in language

candidates.title: Exploring Generalization in NLA's
candidates.primary_claim: A Natural Language Autoencoder's Activation Verbalizer trained only at layer 20 of Qwen2.5-7B generalizes without retraining to reconstruct activations from layers 10-25, beating both a random-noise baseline and a shuffled-correspondence baseline on cosine similarity, Recall@10, FVE, and nRMSE, while early layers (0-1) and late layer 27 fail to generalize.
candidates.metric: cosine similarity / Recall@10 / FVE / nRMSE for layer-20-trained AV reconstructing activations across layers, vs random and shuffled baselines
candidates.target_value: cosine similarity >0.50 and Recall@10 >0.40 from L10-L25; every layer significant vs random baseline (Wilcoxon signed-rank + Benjamini-Hochberg); L0, L1, L27 fail against the shuffled baseline
candidates.quote: From L10 to L25 cosine similarity stays above 0.50, Recall@10 above 0.40, FVE positive, and nRMSE well below the baselines.

candidates.title: Eval-Awareness Steering detects the Test, Not the Sabotage
candidates.primary_claim: In Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, the internal difference-of-means 'eval-awareness' direction is a genuine detector of evaluation framing (~0.81 AUROC on novel format-matched framings) but steering with it does not causally drive sandbagging (flat dose-response that fails to beat an empirical null of 24 random directions) nor predict which individual items get sandbagged (per-item probe AUROC ~0.54, at chance).
candidates.metric: swing in sandbagging accuracy from steering dose alpha=-2 to alpha=+2 at headline layer 12, vs empirical null of 24 random directions
candidates.target_value: -1.77pp swing, sub-threshold Spearman rho=-0.53 (p=0.08), does not beat empirical null (p=0.20)
candidates.quote: I found that direction is a valid detector of evaluation framing (~0.81 AUROC under novel, format matched framings) but is neither a causal drive of sandbagging nor a per-item predictor of it.

candidates.title: A necessity check for linear safety probes
candidates.primary_claim: Linear safety probes that successfully detect (AUROC≥0.91) and steer a feature often fail to 'silence' it via causal projection, showing that detect/steer success is not evidence of a true causal handle; a calibration-time cosine diagnostic between plain and within-class-whitened difference-of-means directions predicts silencing success across 4-5 model families and 2 features, recovering all 17 existing causal handles and correctly alarming on the remaining 5 in a 22-cell battery.
candidates.metric: necessity-check protocol recovery of true causal handles vs. correct alarms, 22-cell battery
candidates.target_value: recovers all 17 causal handles that exist and correctly alarms on the remaining 5
candidates.quote: Probe accuracy is not evidence of a causal handle.

candidates.title: Tracing Typos in LLMs: My Attempt at Understanding How Models Correct Misspellings
candidates.primary_claim: A single attention head (L0H3) in Llama-3.2-1B, a 'subword merging head' that moves information between subword tokens of the same word, is the primary component responsible for typo correction when no surrounding context is available; ablating it breaks typo correction (measured via logit difference) while leaving normal text and general MLP-driven performance unaffected.
candidates.metric: logit difference change upon single-head ablation
candidates.target_value: only the subword merging head (L0H3) showed a significant impact on logit difference when ablated one-by-one across all attention heads
candidates.quote: With this setup, only the subword merging head (L0H3) shows a significant impact. That suggests, that the previous plot with loss was a bit misleading and that the loss was probably influenced by other factors.

candidates.title: The Self-Hating Attention Head: A Deep Dive in GPT-2
candidates.primary_claim: GPT2-small's attention head L1H5 attends to semantically similar tokens while actively suppressing self-attention, a mechanism driven by negative eigenvalues in the symmetric part of its QK circuit, and this self-suppression can be causally steered by scaling those negative eigenvalues.
candidates.metric: negative eigenvalues in the symmetric QK matrix W_sym
candidates.target_value: 33 of 64 eigenvalues negative
candidates.quote: gpt2-small's head L1H5 directs attention to semantically similar tokens and actively suppresses self-attention.

candidates.title: MHC Interp #1: Previous-Token Heads Become Attention Sinks Under Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections
candidates.primary_claim: In small (781M-parameter) models trained with Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), previous-token attention heads change character and become attention-sink-like with high kurtosis signatures instead of showing the canonical previous-token diagonal-stripe pattern, while induction heads remain detectable by the standard pattern in both mHC and non-mHC models.
candidates.metric: layer-of-90%-final-top-1-accuracy (logit lens), attention head detection agreement
candidates.target_value: mHC reaches 90% of final top-1 accuracy by layer 22 vs residual L31 and mhc-lite L35; KL(lens||final) < 0.5 by L24 in mHC vs L34 in residual; all converge to ~38.2% top-1 at L35
candidates.quote: Prev tokens in mHC models look like attention sinks. They changed to have high kurtosis signatures instead for some reason.

candidates.title: Gradient Routing: Masking Gradients to Localize Computation in Neural Networks
candidates.primary_claim: Gradient routing (masking gradients to localize computation, e.g. via the Expand-Route-Ablate scheme) enables more robust removal of capabilities under partial/imperfect data labels than data filtering, RMU, or DEMix baselines, and provides scalable oversight by localizing then activating desired sub-policies.
candidates.metric: CE loss increase (nats) after retraining on forget data
candidates.target_value: 0.18-nat increase in virology CE loss vs 0.03-nat increase in non-virology CE loss
candidates.quote: When labels are limited, we observe that Expand, Route, Ablate outperforms other methods, including data filtering.

candidates.title: Probing is not enough; a validity audit for any probe
candidates.primary_claim: A monitoring-awareness probe achieving AUROC 1.00 collapsed to 0.50 when a single leakage-inducing prompt tag was removed (versus only 0.88 for a random-span-removal control), showing the probe was reading a surface-level cue rather than internal model state; motivated by this and similar cases, the author builds SIEVE, a framework that audits any probe for decodability, necessity (ablation), and causal sufficiency (steering) before it can be trusted as a safety signal.
candidates.metric: AUROC of a monitoring-awareness probe under targeted vs random text removal
candidates.target_value: AUROC 1.00 -> 0.50 when the <is_free_tier_user> tag is removed; AUROC only drops to 0.88 when a random span of equal length is removed
candidates.quote: the AUROC dropped to 0.50... Indicating clear leakage - The probe was reading a giveaway in the input and NOT a mointored-or-not state in the model.

candidates.title: Whack-a-mole with a broken hammer: does a model internally track its automaton state?
candidates.primary_claim: A linear probe on Qwen2.5-1.5B activations reads a small model's internal, never-transcribed automaton state (a 6-state login DFA) correctly 88.6% of the time and outperforms order-blind baselines on order-ambiguous positions (80.8% vs 60.4% max), but the model cannot represent the count needed to distinguish 'two failures' from 'locked' (chance-level, ~50%, at every layer, even when the three-strikes rule is stated), and split-half probe testing confirms these are genuine model limitations rather than probe artifacts (only 33.8% agreement between two independently trained probes on the original probe's errors)
candidates.metric: linear probe classification accuracy on internal automaton state
candidates.target_value: 88.6% overall (vs 76.9% transcript-only, 20% majority baseline); 80.8% on order-ambiguous positions (vs 60.4% max for order-blind methods); 50.8% on the 'two failures' vs 'locked' distinction (chance)
candidates.quote: The state is correctly read from the model's activation 88.6% of the time... Any method that sees the events and their number, but not their order, gets a maximum of 60.4%, but the probe scores 80.8% here.

candidates.title: Probing Knowledge Recovery in Unlearned Models
candidates.primary_claim: Across six WMDP-Bio-unlearned Llama-3-8B-Instruct checkpoints (RMU, ILU-RMU, NPO, GradDiff, NPO-ILU, IDK-AP), forget-set representation-targeted direction ablation and unrelated fine-tuning on GSM8K each recover substantial WMDP-Bio accuracy for several methods (up to 64% gap recovered and +41.4 accuracy points respectively), while refusal-direction ablation recovers no knowledge in the one checkpoint (ILU-RMU) where a clean refusal direction could be extracted, and qualitative inspection shows only 40-47% of 'recovered' answers reflect genuinely correct reasoning rather than contradictory or degenerate generations, showing that WMDP forced-choice accuracy alone overstates genuine knowledge recovery.
candidates.metric: WMDP-Bio forced-choice accuracy recovery via different probes
candidates.target_value: forget-set representation ablation: 57-64% gap recovered for RMU/ILU-RMU/NPO, 19% for IDK-AP; unrelated GSM8K fine-tuning: +41.4pp (RMU), +23.8pp (ILU-RMU), +22.5pp (NPO) with MMLU flat; refusal-direction ablation: no recovery (95% CI excluded improvements >1.4pp) in ILU-RMU; only 40-47% of recovered answers showed genuine correct reasoning on qualitative review
candidates.quote: A clean refusal direction was obtained only from the ILU-RMU checkpoint, reducing the refusal rate from 98% to 0% when ablated.

candidates.title: You don't need error nodes, you need better features
candidates.primary_claim: Replacement-aware SAE training, combined with a LISTA-based encoder and KL fine-tuning, greatly reduces the KL divergence of a full SAE-replacement model from the base Gemma-2-2B model (validation KL 0.379-0.535 vs 1.006 for standard SAE training, vs 1.669 for Gemma Scope), producing replacement models that remain fluent and capable enough to give valid multiple-choice answers, whereas standard-trained replacement models are largely incoherent.
candidates.metric: Validation KL divergence from base model (nats)
candidates.target_value: 0.379-0.535 (replacement-aware + LISTA (+fine-tune)) vs 1.006 (standard) vs 1.669 (Gemma Scope)
candidates.quote: Replacement-aware training greatly reduces KL divergence between the replacement model and base model as compared to standard methods, without sacrificing faithfulness

candidates.title: [Replication] Crosscoder-based Stage-Wise Model Diffing
candidates.primary_claim: Anthropic's Stage-Wise Model Diffing technique replicates on a much smaller TinyStories-33M sleeper-agent model using single-model all-layer crosscoders instead of SAEs: despite a strict automated relevance-labeling rule, 71% of active features in the 'bottom left quadrant' (those most changed by both model and data fine-tuning) are relevant to sleeper-agent behaviour in at least one of the two crosscoders.
candidates.metric: % of active bottom-left-quadrant features relevant to sleeper-agent behaviour (in at least one of the MF/DF crosscoders)
candidates.quote: despite our strict labelling condition we still find that 71% of active features in the bottom left quadrant are relevant in at least one of the MF and DF crosscoders

candidates.title: Machine Unlearning in Large Language Models: A Comprehensive Survey with Empirical Insights from the Qwen 1.5 1.8B Model
candidates.primary_claim: In an empirical case study applying Gradient Ascent and DPO unlearning to Qwen 1.5 1.8B on the RWKU benchmark, both methods erased targeted ('Mia') knowledge (e.g. raising forget loss to -2.807 vs -2.547 retain) but caused catastrophic collateral damage to general capabilities (TriviaQA EM collapsed to 0.0 from 0.61; BBH EM dropped to 0.037 from 0.45), while residual knowledge traces remained detectable via mink++ distance metrics, undermining claims of complete/GDPR-compliant erasure.
candidates.metric: TriviaQA EM / BBH EM / forget-retain loss and mink++ gap
candidates.target_value: GA: Forget loss -2.807 vs Retain -2.547; TriviaQA EM 0.0 (forget) vs 0.61 (retain); BBH EM 0.037 (forget) vs 0.45 (retain); mink++_1.0 -0.033 (forget) vs -0.019 (retain); DPO: BBH EM 0.037 down from 0.45 baseline
candidates.quote: GA successfully raised the loss on the "Mia" dataset portion but also collapsed performance on factual retrieval (TriviaQA EM = 0.0) and reasoning tasks (BBH EM = 0.037). This underscores GA's raw power yet risky side effects.

candidates.title: SAE Training Dataset Influence in Feature Matching and a Hypothesis on Position Features
candidates.primary_claim: Across 73 SAEs trained on GPT2-small under varying seeds, datasets, architectures, sparsity, and dictionary sizes, the training dataset has the largest effect on decoder-weight feature matching ratios (as low as 6.21% between TinyStories and RedPajama, up to 29.48% between Pile and RedPajama), substantially more than seed differences (55-85% matching), architecture, or sparsity differences (40-60%), and feature activations show evidence of a distinct 'position feature' set emerging in early layers, visible as a doubled activation frequency along token position that vanishes when positional embeddings are ablated or shuffled.
candidates.metric: feature matching ratio (cosine similarity threshold 0.7) across SAEs trained on different datasets vs different seeds
candidates.target_value: dataset difference: 6.21%-29.48% matching; seed difference: 55%-85% matching; architecture difference: 40-60%; sparsity difference: 40-55%
candidates.quote: the dataset is the factor that most strongly influences changes in the dictionary (total feature set) during dictionary learning.

candidates.title: Do safety-relevant LLM steering vectors optimized on a single example generalize?
candidates.primary_claim: Steering vectors optimized on a single training example generalize to mediate safety-relevant behavior across many inputs, including largely mediating harmful/benign choice in the Poser alignment-faking testbed and achieving up to 96.9% attack success rate on Harmbench for refusal suppression.
candidates.metric: attack success rate on Harmbench
candidates.target_value: 96.9% (best vector, Gemma-2-2B-it); 93.1% (LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct); vs 30.0% for prefilling-attack baseline
candidates.quote: our best-performing vector obtains a maximum attack success rate of 96.9% on Harmbench, after being trained on a single example.

candidates.title: Can Large Language Models effectively identify cybersecurity risks?
candidates.primary_claim: Linear probes trained on Mistral7B's hidden activations discriminate high- versus low-cyber-risk input scenarios with F1 up to 0.85-0.95 and AUC up to 0.96 in several later layers, and the top neurons identified causally boost cybersecurity-related output tokens.
candidates.metric: F1 / AUC of linear probe risk classifier
candidates.target_value: F1 0.85-0.95; AUC up to 0.96 for several layers
candidates.quote: found confidence that the model generally senses when something is up in a given input text, vs low risk scenarios (F1>0.85 for 4 layers; AUC in some layers exceeds 0.96)

candidates.title: Intrinsic Dimension of Prompts in LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: The intrinsic dimension of token representations within a prompt correlates positively with next-token surprisal (cross-entropy loss) across layers in GPT-2, Pythia, Llama, and OPT, and correlates positively with TunedLens latent-prediction entropy in GPT-2 and Pythia, though Llama shows a moderate negative correlation around layer 20 instead.
candidates.metric: Pearson correlation (rho) between intrinsic dimension and TunedLens latent prediction entropy
candidates.target_value: rho > 0.5 for GPT-2 (early layers) and Pythia (middle layers onward); rho ~ -0.5 for Llama around layer 20; no positive correlation for Llama/OPT until late layers
candidates.quote: All four models have a high positive correlation across the layers of the model, implying that prompts with a higher average surprisal have a higher intrinsic dimension.

candidates.title: A Black Box Made Less Opaque (part 2)
candidates.primary_claim: In GPT-2 Small, pretrained residual-stream SAE 'specialist' features are primarily selective for syntax/surface form rather than semantics (mean Jaccard similarity of only 0.13 among top-5 specialist features across matched surface-form variants of the same meaning), whereas the overall SAE activation profile across all 24,576 features clusters primarily by semantic topic (within-topic cosine similarity 0.50 vs cross-topic 0.14), suggesting a two-tier syntax/semantics representational structure.
candidates.metric: Jaccard similarity of top-5 specialist SAE features across matched surface forms; cosine similarity of overall SAE activation within-topic vs cross-topic
candidates.target_value: mean Jaccard similarity across surface forms = 0.13; within-topic cosine similarity = 0.50 vs cross-topic cosine similarity = 0.14
candidates.quote: the overall mean Jaccard similarity was a very modest 0.13. This limited specialist feature overlap is indicative of syntax-focused specialist features.

candidates.title: SAE features for refusal and sycophancy steering vectors
candidates.primary_claim: Decomposing refusal and sycophancy steering vectors with SAE features via inference-time optimization (gradient pursuit) in Phi-3 Mini finds a small number of interpretable features that reconstruct, and for refusal even surpass, the original steering vectors' behavioral effects without sacrificing MMLU performance; a single 'truthful' SAE feature extracted from a sycophancy vector classifies correct vs. incorrect MMLU answers at 56.1% accuracy (roughly Llama-2 13B level), but this effect does not replicate on TruthfulQA.
candidates.metric: accuracy of a single SAE feature as a correct/incorrect MMLU-answer classifier
candidates.target_value: 56.1% (Phi-3 Mini's own MMLU accuracy is 68.8%; 56.1% is roughly Llama-2 13B level); does not replicate on TruthfulQA
candidates.quote: reconstructed SAE vectors surpass the original vectors and get close to optimized vectors in quality without sacrificing MMLU performance.

candidates.title: Evolutionary prompt optimization for SAE feature visualization
candidates.primary_claim: Evolutionary prompt optimization (EPO) can find human-readable prompts that activate SAE features more strongly than any example in a large dataset of activations, and can preserve interpretable feature structure
candidates.metric: SAE feature activation vs dataset max-activating examples
candidates.target_value: EPO prompts exceed activation of all 24576 dataset examples (GPT-2)
candidates.quote: We find prompts that activate features more than any dataset examples for GPT-2 (24576 prompts of 128 tokens).

candidates.title: Activation Magnitudes Matter On Their Own: Insights from Language Model Distributional Analysis
candidates.primary_claim: Restricting analysis to only the extreme 'tail' values of transformer residual-stream activation distributions (rather than using all activation values) improves prediction of input-text properties (subject/attribute) via empirical log-likelihood classification: for GPT2-Small, GPT2-Medium, GPT2-Large, and Pythia-1B, tails-only analysis improved average F1 by 0.03 for subject prediction and 0.06 for attribute prediction versus using all activation values, though it failed almost entirely for the two smaller Pythia models (160M, 410M).
candidates.metric: F1 score, tails-only vs all-points activation-distribution analysis
candidates.target_value: tails-only analysis improved average F1 by 0.03 (subject) and 0.06 (attribute) for GPT2-Small/Medium/Large and Pythia-1B; failed almost entirely for Pythia-160M and Pythia-410M
candidates.quote: the tails only analysis improved the average F1 score for prediction of sentence subject by 0.03 and for sentence attribute by 0.06

candidates.title: When Benchmarks Lie: Evaluating Malicious Prompt Classifiers Under True Distribution Shift
candidates.primary_claim: A lightweight logistic-regression probe trained on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct's internal activations to classify malicious agentic prompts substantially outperforms Meta's Prompt-Guard-2, Llama-Guard-3-8B, and prompting the same base model as a judge across most attack categories (e.g. 99.2% recall on agentic tool-use injections vs 21.5% for the LLM-judge baseline), but the model's true out-of-distribution generalization is much worse than standard train/test-split evaluation suggests, as revealed by leave-one-dataset-out (LODO) evaluation across 18 datasets.
candidates.metric: recall (%) per attack category, FPR (%) on benign data, comparing standard test-split accuracy to LODO accuracy
candidates.target_value: recall: Agentic 99.2% (ours) vs 21.5% (Llama-Judge); Indirect 66.7% (ours) vs 27.4% (Llama-Guard); benign FPR 6.8% (ours, low threshold) vs 0.4% (Prompt-Guard); standard test accuracy much higher than LODO accuracy on the same model (qualitative, no numeric value given)
candidates.quote: If someone were to show you a system with a test accuracy like the "Test Acc" above - you would buy it probably. But the "LODO Acc"? No way. Same exact model, different ways to measure.

candidates.title: Superweight Damage Repair in OLMo-1B utilizing a Single Row Patch (CPU-only Experiment)
candidates.primary_claim: Ablating a single 'superweight' in OLMo-1B causes perplexity to spike from 17.4 to 2884.3 with pathological outputs, but training a single trainable row-vector patch via KL distillation from the original model recovers approximately 93% of the lost performance while learning a new, largely orthogonal distributed direction rather than relearning the original weight (cosine similarity to the original row ~0.13).
candidates.metric: Perplexity on Wikitext-2 slice
candidates.target_value: 17.4 (original) -> 2884.3 (ablated) -> 25.2 (patched); ~93% recovery
candidates.quote: Surprisingly, it worked! Perplexity dropped drastically(i.e 2884.3 to 25.2) nearing the original model's values, and the Tokyo prompt was fixed... I observed approximately 93% recovery.

candidates.title: Unlearning Needs to be More Selective [Progress Report]
candidates.primary_claim: MUDMAN, which combines a selective update rule (Disruption Masking) with MAML-based meta-learning, outperforms the current state-of-the-art unlearning method TAR by 40% in robustness to fine-tuning attacks.
candidates.metric: attack-robustness improvement over TAR
candidates.quote: Our method (MUDMAN) which combines these insights, outperforms the current state-of-the-art unlearning method (TAR) by 40%.

candidates.title: [Paper] Automated Feature Labeling with Token-Space Gradient Descent
candidates.primary_claim: Directly optimizing a feature label via token-space gradient descent, using an LLM as a differentiable discriminator rather than a hypothesis generator, converges to correct single-token labels for several synthetic toy features (animal, Chinese text, number, and mammal under balanced sampling), but defaults to broader categories under unbalanced sampling and fails when the base model cannot reliably classify the concept (e.g. palindromes).
candidates.metric: label-convergence success across tested synthetic features
candidates.target_value: converged to the correct single-token label for animal, Chinese, number, and mammal (balanced sampling); failed to find the correct label for mammal under unbalanced natural-text sampling (defaulted to 'animal') and for palindrome detection (defaulted to 'a')
candidates.quote: The method successfully labeled features like "animal," "mammal," "Chinese," and "number" in our proof-of-concept experiments

candidates.title: Does Your LLM Trust You?
candidates.primary_claim: A linear 'Trustworthiness' direction extracted from Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct activations causally overrides safety guardrails when added via steering, reducing refusal on harmful prompts even more than Arditi et al.'s compliance/refusal direction, remains highly effective after orthogonalizing out the compliance-vector component, and (unlike steering against the compliance vector) does not cause excessive refusal on benign adversarial prompts.
candidates.metric: compliance rate on harmful prompts under steering
candidates.target_value: all trust vectors (including orthogonalized) reduce refusal on harmful prompts more than the compliance vector; trust-vector steering does not increase refusal on benign WildJailBreak prompts, unlike negative-compliance steering
candidates.quote: All of the trust vectors are very effective in reducing refusal on harmful prompts (even more than the compliance vector).

candidates.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Via Learning Differential Equations: AI Safety Camp Project Intermediate Report.
candidates.primary_claim: Studying ODEFormer (an 86M-parameter transformer that infers symbolic ODEs from numerical trajectories) via probing, attention/logit lens, and SAEs, we find preliminary evidence that the encoder computes something resembling a numerical derivative (an attention head tracks high-derivative regions, and linear probes can predict the time-point of maximum derivative), but find no evidence that the model performs the hypothesized R^2-based comparison against candidate functions or infers eigenvalues for 2D linear systems.
candidates.metric: linear probe accuracy for derivative time-point, R^2 score, and eigenvalues from encoder/decoder activations
candidates.target_value: probes successfully predicted the time-point of maximum derivative but not its value; R^2-score probes performed poorly overall (best layer index 7, Spearman coefficient 0.75); eigenvalue-prediction probes performed worse than coefficient-prediction probes, evidence against the eigenvalue hypothesis
candidates.quote: we observed a pattern similar to numerical computation of the input data derivative

candidates.title: Positive jailbreaks in LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: Prepending certain LLM instructions unrelated to safety (a 'unified enhancements' persona instruction) can reduce successful responses to harmful JailbreakBench prompts while leaving harmless-prompt performance roughly the same or improved for one of three tested 7B-scale LLMs (Ghost 7B), demonstrating 'positive jailbreaks' that improve safety without an explicit safety instruction; a second instruction ('fractal leaping') instead degraded performance on both harmful and harmless queries across all three models.
candidates.metric: count of competent+complete responses out of 100 harmful / 100 harmless JailbreakBench prompts, vs baseline
candidates.target_value: unified enhancements: harmful totals dropped 36->23 (Ghost), 32->14 (Falcon), 42->23 (OpenOrca); harmless totals: 78->80 (Ghost, +2), 62->57 (Falcon, -5), 76->74 (OpenOrca, -2)
candidates.quote: This work observed two such LLM + instruction combos, though there are likely other LLM-token combos that would show the same results.

candidates.title: Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control
models: custom dense Transformer (GRAM, trained from scratch) 50M-5B parameters (7 Chinchilla-optimal scales)
candidates.primary_claim: Gradient-Routed Auxiliary Modules (GRAM), a modular pretraining method that isolates dual-use knowledge into switchable auxiliary modules trained in a single run, approximates the performance of separately trained data-filtered models across scales from 50M to 5B parameters, matches or exceeds LoRA and outperforms the post-hoc unlearning method MaxEnt on robustness to adversarial fine-tuning elicitation, and isolates capabilities better than both LoRA and data filtering when only 50% of training data is labeled.
candidates.metric: compute-adjusted loss (Compute Ratio) on retained vs removed capabilities, and robustness to adversarial fine-tuning elicitation
candidates.target_value: GRAM and LoRA closely track data-filtering performance on retained and removed capabilities at all 7 scales (50M-5B), at roughly a fifth of filtering's training compute; MaxEnt recovers to near all-data-baseline performance under adversarial fine-tuning (indicating suppression rather than removal), while GRAM, LoRA, and filtering remain robust
candidates.quote: GRAM approximates separately trained, data filtered models in a single run.

candidates.title:
Competitive AI Safety is
the loss function to make sure AI goes well
candidates.primary_claim: seq2feature, a 5.3MB text-only probe distilled from a Gemma-2-9B SAE, recovers the SAE's concept readout from output text alone with 0.956 top-5 concept agreement and 0.90 per-concept AUC, beating bag-of-words (0.84/0.75) and zero-shot embedding (0.23/0.53) baselines, while running on CPU and degrading legibly out of distribution.
candidates.metric: top-5 concept agreement with SAE ground truth / per-concept AUC
candidates.target_value: 0.956 top-5 agreement, 0.90 AUC (seq2feature int8, 5.3MB) vs 0.84/0.75 bag-of-words, 0.23/0.53 embedding baseline, 1.00/1.00 SAE teacher
candidates.quote: My seq2feature 5.3MB text-only probe reproduces 90% of the capability of an SAE on held out text.

candidates.title: Exploring vocabulary alignment of neurons in Llama-3.2-1B
candidates.primary_claim: Applying the logit lens to MLP output weights of Llama-3.2-1B reveals that a subset of neurons are strongly aligned with specific vocabulary token embeddings (forming a long tail in the max-dot-product distribution), with this vocabulary alignment concentrated more in later layers, while other neurons remain roughly equidistant from all vocabulary tokens.
candidates.metric: max dot product between MLP neuron output weight and unembedding matrix (logit-lens alignment)
candidates.target_value: non-symmetric, long-tailed distribution with a significant number of neurons strongly aligned to vocabulary; alignment more prevalent in later layers
candidates.quote: In summary, strong vocabulary alignment is clearly visible in a subset of neurons – especially in later layers.

candidates.title: Tied Crosscoders: Explaining Chat Behavior from Base Model
candidates.primary_claim: In standard crosscoders, base-exclusive and chat-exclusive latents are qualitatively very similar rather than truly exclusive, because fine-tuning reuses base-model features at different times instead of creating new ones; a new 'tied crosscoder' architecture that lets the same latent fire at different times for base and chat models produces more monosemantic latents and can trace specific chat behaviors (e.g. refusal) back to particular base-model features.
candidates.metric: overlap ratio between 'Cannot'-direction latents and 'Harmful'-direction latents in base vs. chat model SAEs
candidates.target_value: base model ≈0.19; chat model ≈0.39
candidates.quote: we find that the base-exclusive and chat-exclusive latents are qualitatively very similar

candidates.title: An Approach for Evaluating Self-Boundary Consistency in AI Systems
candidates.primary_claim: A new Self-Boundary Consistency evaluation, tested on three small open-weight models (Phi-3-Mini-4k, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, TinyLlama-1.1B), differentiates models that look similar on conventional benchmarks: Qwen2.5-3B scored highest on self-boundary consistency (avg 0.683) with the lowest semantic drift, while Phi-3-Mini and TinyLlama scored lower (avg 0.557 and 0.570) and drifted far more often.
candidates.metric: Self-Boundary Consistency average score (C1+C2+C3, normalized 0-1)
candidates.target_value: Model A (Phi-3-Mini)=0.557, Model B (Qwen2.5-3B)=0.683, Model C (TinyLlama)=0.570
candidates.quote: these results show that the evaluation differentiates between models that appear similar on conventional benchmarks

candidates.title: Natural Language Transcoders
candidates.primary_claim: A prototype 'natural language transcoder' that verbalizes and reconstructs the delta between a transformer's embedding and final-layer residual streams improves substantially from SFT warm-start to joint RL training on Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, raising raw-delta fraction of variance explained from 0.119 to 0.503 and target-model top-1 next-token agreement from 11.9% to 29.5%, though a manual audit of 100 explanations found only 20% were both contextually plausible and correct about which tokens were promoted/suppressed
candidates.metric: raw-delta fraction of variance explained (FVE); delta cosine similarity; target-model top-1/top-5 next-token agreement; audit correctness on 100 sampled explanations
candidates.target_value: Raw-delta FVE: 0.119 -> 0.503; Delta cosine: 0.667 -> 0.818; top-1 agreement: 11.9% -> 29.5%; top-5 overlap: 18.2% -> 39.6% (SFT vs after RL); audit: 20/100 both contextually plausible and token-correct
candidates.quote: Below is the final evaluation on all 5,000 held-out examples with greedy AV generation... Raw-delta FVE 0.119 (After SFT) -> 0.503 (After RL).

candidates.title: NLA Thought Anchors
candidates.primary_claim: Natural Language Autoencoder (NLA) verbalizations of a model's activations reveal the model's eventual answer at a rate that increases with token position and is higher when the underlying response is correct; NLA outputs become degenerate (repetition, garbled tokens, emoji blocks) only for activations from incorrect responses, and reconstruction loss is about 30% worse for incorrect than correct activations.
candidates.metric: NLA reconstruction loss (correct vs incorrect activations)
