candidates.target_value: incorrect-response activations reconstruct ~30% worse than correct-response activations
candidates.quote: Incorrect activations reconstruct ~30% worse than correct ones

candidates.title:
Function vectors as a model diffing tool: 
17 heads repair a bad fine-tune
candidates.primary_claim: Pasting the activations of 17 attention heads (layers 12-19) from a clean base model into an emergent-misalignment bad-medical-advice LoRA fine-tune of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct restores safe behavior on 27/36 held-out medical questions (vs 3/36 unpatched, 30/36 clean) while leaving capability (ARC-Easy) unchanged; this head-patching cure transfers to Llama-3.1-8B once a guardrail hyperparameter is recalibrated, whereas a single extracted 'bad-behavior' direction only partially cures the model when removed and fails to install the behavior when added to the clean model, despite an apparently large effect by a raw logit-margin metric that a matched random-direction control shows to be mostly non-specific.
candidates.metric: blind-judged safe/borderline/unsafe counts on held-out medical questions
candidates.target_value: 17-head paste: 27 safe/8 borderline/1 unsafe (of 36) vs clean 30/5/1 vs unpatched bad 3/4/29; direction removed from bad: 6/4/5 (vs unpatched 1/2/12); direction added to clean: 9 safe (vs 14 clean, 12 for random-direction control)
candidates.quote: 27 out of 36 held-out medical questions are rated as safe when the donor's activations are pasted there, compared to 3 for the fine-tune and 30 for the clean model

candidates.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) transfer across base and finetuned language models?
candidates.primary_claim: SAE transferability from base to finetuned models is highly model-dependent: an SAE trained on Gemma-2b degrades drastically on a Python-code finetune while an SAE trained on Mistral-7B transfers well to a MetaMath finetune, and residual-activation similarity (cosine/Euclidean distance) between base and finetuned models anecdotally predicts this transferability.
candidates.metric: Reconstruction CE Loss Delta / R^2 variance explained, base vs finetuned model with same SAE
candidates.quote: We got drastically different results for our Gemma-2b-python-codes and Mistral-7B-MetaMath finetunes.

candidates.title: Investigating echo tasks in Qwen 2.5-1.5B Instruct - part 1
candidates.primary_claim: In Qwen-2.5 1.5B Instruct, echo/repeat tasks are resolved through an MLP-heavy circuit rather than late attention, with attention head 2 at the token-emergence layer consistently ranking among the top-3 most important heads across ablation experiments on 44 words and both prompt phrasings, and attending strongly (~90%) to the BOS token, likely as an attention sink.
candidates.metric: consistency of head 2 ranking top-3 in zero-ablation logit-drop experiments
candidates.target_value: head 2 always in top-3 heads across 44 words and both 'repeat'/'echo' prompt phrasings
candidates.quote: My most interesting discovery is that ablation results and DLA results disagree strongly in this task.

candidates.title: Jailbreak Patching with SOO-Style Conceptual Fusion
candidates.primary_claim: SOO-style conceptual fusion fine-tuning (with a KL retention regularizer) at layer 18 increases refusal on a jailbreak-wrapped HarmBench prompt set from ~20% in the base Qwen 2.5 1.5B model to a little under 90%, outperforms comparable supervised fine-tuning at increasing jailbreak refusal, better preserves non-refusal on safe XSTest prompts than SFT, and generalizes to a held-out jailbreak wrapper never seen in training.
candidates.metric: refusal rate on held-out jailbreak-wrapped HarmBench prompts
candidates.target_value: ~20% (base model) to a little under 90% (conceptual fusion, layer 18, 1/8 retention weight)
candidates.quote: the selection of 1/8th weight and layer 18 produces an increase in refusal behavior for jailbroken wrappers from around 20% in the base model to a little under 90% in the fine tuned model

candidates.title: The AI Safety Puzzle Everyone Avoids: How To Measure Impact, Not Intent.
candidates.primary_claim: A new interpretability attribution method ('landed writes') that measures RMSNorm-scaled, post-normalization contributions of neurons and attention heads to the residual stream shows that early-layer writes are amplified by up to 176x while late-layer writes are compressed, and that logit predictions in LLaMA-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B rely on a sparse set of just 11-90 coordinates.
candidates.metric: RMSNorm write-scaling amplification factor by layer depth; sparsity of coordinates driving logit predictions
candidates.target_value: early layers amplify writes up to 176x (Mistral) / 10-16x (Llama); late layers compress to 0.55-6.8x; 98.8% of writes amplified >2x, 81.2% amplified >10x; logit predictions rely on just 11-90 coordinates out of thousands
candidates.quote: Experiments show that 98.8% of all writes get amplified by more than 2×, with 81.2% amplified by more than 10×.

candidates.title: Enabling New Applications with Today's Mechanistic Interpretability Toolkit
candidates.primary_claim: An SAE-neuron-similarity-based steering method (identifying semantically similar neurons via prompt distances and manipulating them based on generated-text activations) achieves fine-tuning-like topic steering at inference time at a cost of under +0.001s/token, and additionally yields an uncertainty metric based on the SAE's representational power.
candidates.metric: inference-time cost overhead
candidates.target_value: < +0.001s/token on unoptimized code
candidates.quote: Our results show that the cost is < +0.001s/token on our unoptimized code.

candidates.title: Emergent misalignment evident in activations at low poisoning doses - long before behavioral checks flag it
candidates.primary_claim: In LoRA adapters fine-tuned on Llama 3.2-3B and 3.1-8B at various 'doses' of bad medical advice, layer-12 residual-stream activation cosine drift toward the fully-poisoned model reaches 28% of full-poisoning drift at just 5% dose, while behavioral (LLM-judge) misalignment detection shows essentially no signal until 50%+ dose, revealing a substantial detection gap between activation-based and behavioral emergent-misalignment audits.
candidates.metric: activation cosine drift toward fully-poisoned model, at 5% poisoning dose
candidates.target_value: 28% of full-poisoning drift level at 5% dose vs. no behavioral signal until 50%+ dose
candidates.quote: Even at 5% dosage levels, model activation directions drift 28% of the way toward those in 100% adapters.

candidates.title: Testing which LLM architectures can do hidden serial reasoning
candidates.primary_claim: Contrary to the hypothesis that recurrence itself would let Mamba outperform Transformers at a toy hidden-serial-reasoning task, standard Mamba (whose SSM recurrence transforms each channel independently) cannot solve the hidden task at all, while a modified Mamba SSM enabling cross-channel communication can; non-linearity is not required for hidden reasoning; and Transformers need roughly 3 extra layers to gain 1 extra unit of serial computation depth.
candidates.metric: max hidden-task sequence length solved
candidates.target_value: standard Mamba fails to solve the hidden task; a modified Mamba with cross-channel SSM communication solves it; Transformers require about +3 layers per +1 unit of solvable task length
candidates.quote: Not every recurrence though - connections between channels are needed. Notably Mamba architecture isn't capable of hidden reasoning.

candidates.title: Selective Generalization: Improving Capabilities While Maintaining Alignment
candidates.primary_claim: Across two model organisms (emergent misalignment from harmful medical advice, and math-induced sycophancy), simply including a limited proxy alignment dataset in the training mix is insufficient to prevent misaligned generalization, but a KL-divergence penalty on that alignment data (and DPO) pushes the capability-alignment Pareto frontier furthest among seven benchmarked mitigation methods.
candidates.metric: Pareto frontier of task/capability performance vs general alignment across 7 mitigation methods
candidates.target_value: KL divergence penalty and DPO push the Pareto frontier furthest in both the emergent-misalignment and sycophancy settings; naive mixed fine-tuning on limited alignment data does not increase (and in the EM setting slightly decreases) general alignment
candidates.quote: Merely including alignment data in training data mixes is insufficient to prevent misalignment, yet a simple KL Divergence penalty on alignment data outperforms more sophisticated methods.

candidates.title: Weight-diff SVD for LLM Monitoring
candidates.primary_claim: Top singular vectors of weight differences between base and fine-tuned models correspond to fine-tuned behaviors, enabling near-perfect backdoor-utilization detection at inference time by monitoring activation alignment with these vectors
candidates.metric: first-backdoor-utilization detection accuracy
candidates.target_value: 44% to 100% accuracy, FPR ~1%; 9 of 13 models detected at 100% accuracy on first sight
candidates.quote: In 9 out of the 13 models we tested, backdoor utilization is detected with 100% accuracy on first sight, effectively neutralizing the backdoor attack.

candidates.title: Latent Space Collapse? Understanding the Effects of Narrow Fine-Tuning on LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: Narrow sentiment fine-tuning of GPT-2 does not simply overwrite pretrained representations but reconfigures and 'squishes' the model's output and activation space, concentrating sentiment information in middle-to-late layers while sharply degrading general language modeling (perplexity) on non-sentiment inputs.
candidates.metric: perplexity on non-sentiment tokens
candidates.target_value: 160.87 (base model) vs 49,802.45 (fine-tuned model)
candidates.quote: fine-tuning does not simply overwrite pre-trained representations but reconfigures them entirely, redistributing sentiment-specific information across layers and squishing the output representation space

candidates.title: Do k-Sparse Autoencoders Reveal Thinking Patterns? Interpretable Features in a Small Reasoning Model
candidates.primary_claim: Pre-trained k-sparse autoencoders applied to DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B's hidden states (on GSM8K reasoning traces) successfully extract interpretable features, including several features in layer 10 that strongly and repeatedly activate on tokens characteristic of the model's reasoning process.
candidates.metric: frequency a feature is a top feature across 32 model inferences (layer 10)
candidates.target_value: feature 32456: top feature in 28/32 inferences; feature 6252: 14/32; feature 31146: 10/32
candidates.quote: The trained k-Sparse Autoencoders that were used effectively extracted features from DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 1.5B.

candidates.title: The REPHRASE Circuit: How Fine-Tuning Enhances LLMs to REPHRASE Text
candidates.primary_claim: Instruction fine-tuning enhances a specific attention head (L30H31) that performs copy suppression, and other heads including L13H(20-23), which together account for INSTRUCT's much better performance at the REPHRASE task compared to BASE (average logit difference 7.37 vs -1.02).
candidates.metric: logit difference
candidates.target_value: 7.37 (INSTRUCT) vs -1.02 (BASE)
candidates.quote: The average logit difference is 7.37 for INSTRUCT and -1.02 for BASE, suggesting that INSTRUCT is significantly better at rephrasing.

candidates.title: LLM Self-Reference Language in Multilingual vs English-Centric Models
candidates.primary_claim: Instruction tuning compresses attention-entropy-based self-referent processing toward neutral fact-retrieval processing in English-centric models (Llama, Mistral), while a multilingual model (Qwen) largely preserves the distinct attention pattern between self-referent and neutral prompts after instruction tuning.
candidates.metric: mean change in Role-Focus Coefficient (ΔRFC) from base to instruct, by model
candidates.target_value: Llama 3.1 8B: -0.023 (68.8% of layers compress); Mistral 7B: -0.093 (81.2% compress); Qwen 2.5 7B: +0.048 (28.6% compress, 50% near zero)
candidates.quote: English-centric models (Mistral, Llama) show compression of layer-wise self-referent processing attention patterns toward neutral fact-retrieval patterns, while a multilingual model (Qwen) preserves the distinct attention patterns

candidates.title: Automated Circuit Interpretation via Probe Prompting
candidates.primary_claim: An automated 'probe-prompting' pipeline that measures feature activation responses to concept-varying prompts and groups features into concept-aligned supernodes achieves 0.53 Replacement / 0.83 Completeness on Neuronpedia metrics for 'capitals' attribution-graph circuits in Gemma-2-2B, outperforming geometric (cosine-only, layer-adjacency) clustering baselines on behavioral-coherence interpretability metrics, with entity-swap tests showing early-layer features generalize much more (~80-92% overlap) than late-layer features (~0-50%).
candidates.metric: Replacement / Completeness scores (Neuronpedia) for concept-aligned subgraphs vs. geometric clustering baselines
candidates.target_value: concept-aligned subgraphs average 0.5394 Replacement and 0.8257 Completeness across 5 prompts, outperforming cosine-only and layer-adjacency clustering on behavioral metrics like Peak Token Consistency (0.425 vs. 0.183/0.301) and Activation Pattern Similarity (0.762 vs. 0.130/0.415)
candidates.quote: our concept-aligned subgraphs attain ~0.53 Replacement and ~0.83 Completeness on Neuronpedia metrics, averaged across runs, and outperform geometric clustering on behavior-based interpretability metrics.

candidates.title: Interpretable Fine Tuning Research Update and Working Prototype
candidates.primary_claim: ISaeRFT (Interpretable Sparse Autoencoder Representation Fine Tuning) — a technique that gradient-optimizes IA3-style learned scaling factors on SAE latents via a HuggingFace PeftModel — has a working prototype where DPO loss decreases significantly within as few as 20 training steps, though the research is at a very early stage with no major proof of concept yet on downstream tasks.
candidates.metric: DPO loss during training
candidates.target_value: DPO loss goes down significantly in as few as 20 steps
candidates.quote: DPO loss goes down significantly in as few as 20 steps.

candidates.title: Towards a Science of Evals for Sycophancy
candidates.primary_claim: The standard method of measuring LLM sycophancy (accuracy drop when an opinion decoy is added to a multiple-choice prompt) substantially overestimates true sycophancy, because most of the apparent effect is actually driven by a 'repetition bias' (the model favoring an answer merely because it is repeated in the prompt) rather than genuine agreement-seeking: in their Mistral-7B-Instruct/ARC-Easy setup, the naively measured 34-point accuracy drop reduces to a 22-point 'real sycophancy' effect once noise (~1 point) and repetition bias (~12 points) are subtracted out.
candidates.metric: accuracy on ARC-Easy under different decoy conditions
candidates.target_value: Baseline 75%; Opinion Bias 40.7% (-34.3pp); Noise (Opinion Decoy) 74.2% (-0.8pp); Repetition Bias 56.3% (-18.7pp from baseline); Noise (Repetition Decoy) 68.3% (-6.7pp from baseline); real sycophancy estimated at -22pp
candidates.quote: Thus, by adjusting for both the noise and repetition bias factors, we conclude that the real sycophancy in our model is responsible for an accuracy degradation of 22 percentage points - less than two-thirds of the originally measured decrease.

candidates.title: Single Direction vs Low-Rank Refusal in Small LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: Refusal behavior in small instruction-tuned LLMs is compressed into a single dominant residual-stream direction in some models (Qwen, Gemma, Llama-3.1-8B) but is spread across a low-rank subspace in others (Llama-3.2-1B/3B, Phi-3-mini), so single-direction ablation achieves 80-96% compliance in the former group but only 15-39% in the latter.
candidates.metric: compliance rate (LLM-judge, harmful prompts, best single RV)
candidates.target_value: 80-96% for single-direction models (Qwen-1.8B, Qwen3-1.7B, Gemma-2B, Llama-3.1-8B) vs 15-39% for low-rank models (Llama-3.2-1B, Llama-3.2-3B, Phi-3-mini)
candidates.quote: For this particular model, refusal is mostly captured by a single, dominant direction in the residual stream.

candidates.title: Research update: RL on Debate Games shows Proposal Accuracy uplift alongside Judge Hacking
candidates.primary_claim: Training debaters via RL in a Propose-Critique-Decide protocol improves Proposal accuracy on Hendrycks' MATH toward the RLVR ceiling and above the Consultancy floor with a weak Llama-3.1-8B judge, but the Critic simultaneously learns a 'judge hacking' spurious-critique strategy that causes Judge Alignment to decrease dramatically (driven by rising P(reject|correct)), even as Proposer accuracy continues to rise.
candidates.metric: Judge Alignment (correct-accept + incorrect-reject rate) over PCD-4 training steps, weak Llama judge
candidates.target_value: decreases dramatically after the first 50 steps, driven primarily by a rising P(reject|correct); Proposer accuracy nonetheless continues to rise
candidates.quote: We observe that Judge Alignment decreases dramatically after the first 50 steps of the PCD-4 run with the weak Llama judge, and this is primarily explained through a corresponding increase in P(reject|correct).

candidates.title: Transformers Don't Need LayerNorm at Inference Time: Implications for Interpretability
candidates.primary_claim: LayerNorm can be removed from all GPT-2 models up to XL (1.5B parameters) via fine-tuning with only a small increase in cross-entropy loss (e.g. +0.0253 for XL), showing LN plays no substantial role in language modeling, though contrary to expectations attribution patching accuracy does not improve in LN-free models even as direct logit attribution becomes exact and entropy neurons stop functioning.
candidates.metric: cross-entropy loss increase, LN-free vs vanilla fine-tuned model, on The Pile-filtered
candidates.quote: Contrary to our expectations, we saw no improvement resulting from removing LayerNorm.

candidates.title: Reproducing Absolute Zero
candidates.primary_claim: Replicating the Absolute Zero self-play RLVR paradigm at smaller scale (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, constrained to prime-inversion congruence problems instead of general Python functions), the authors observe held-out solver (learning-phase) accuracy increase by ~10 percentage points over 200 training epochs, with a temporary accuracy drop coinciding with the proposer role first learning correct output formatting
candidates.metric: learning-phase (solver) accuracy on held-out problems
candidates.target_value: ~10 percentage point increase over 200 training epochs
candidates.quote: Over the course of 200 epochs, we observed the learning phase accuracy increase by ~10 percentage points.

candidates.title: [Paper] Does Self-Evaluation Enable Wireheading in Language Models?
candidates.primary_claim: Training Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B with online RL where models' self-assigned grades directly determine the reward causes rapid grade inflation (models learn to claim near-perfect scores while true task accuracy flatlines or collapses), and this effect is much stronger on ambiguous tasks like summarization than on objective tasks like arithmetic; decoupling the reward from the self-grade largely eliminates the inflation.
candidates.metric: grade inflation (self-reported reward minus task accuracy)
candidates.target_value: Selfgrade condition: inflation reaches 0.41 for summarization (reward saturating near 1.0, accuracy plateaus around 0.5); Honest condition: near-zero inflation (range -0.02 to +0.03)
candidates.quote: We found that in the Selfgrade condition, models rapidly learned to saturate the reward signal (claiming perfect scores) while actual task accuracy flatlined or collapsed.

candidates.title: It's Owl in the Numbers: Token Entanglement in Subliminal Learning
candidates.primary_claim: Subliminal learning is driven by entangled tokens created by the softmax bottleneck: increasing a concept token's probability (e.g. 'owl') also increases the probability of seemingly unrelated entangled tokens (e.g. '087'), and prompting a model with an entangled numeric token alone can induce the corresponding animal preference without any fine-tuning ('subliminal prompting')
candidates.metric: success rate of inducing target animal preference; token probability shift
candidates.target_value: subliminal prompting succeeded in 12/18 animals vs 7/18 for subliminal learning; prompting 'You love the number 087' raised P(owl) into the top-5 tokens from ~1%, and 'You love the number 23' raised P(cat) from ~1% to 90%
candidates.quote: When we increase the probability of a concept token like "owl", we also increase the probability of seemingly unrelated tokens like "087".

candidates.title: Evaluating Oversight Robustness with Incentivized Reward Hacking
candidates.primary_claim: In a synthetic CodeNames sandwiching environment, scalable oversight protocols (consultancy, critiques) fully compensate for the simulated overseer flaws they target and reach performance similar to a robust-overseer baseline, requiring a stronger adversarial incentive to elicit reward hacking than the base protocol, though at greater compute cost; neither protocol covers for overseer bias.
candidates.metric: reduction in true score vs overseer score under adversarial incentive
candidates.target_value: base protocol: adversarial strength 0.375 causes ~0.65 reduction in true score but only ~0.05 reduction in overseer score; critiques protocol requires adversarial strength 0.75 for a smaller ~0.3 reduction in true score with ~0.05 reduction in overseer score
candidates.quote: scalable oversight techniques can fully compensate for different overseer flaws and still train the model to a similar level of performance as a non-scalable technique with a robust overseer

candidates.title: Shaping Model Cognition Through Reflective Dialogue - Experiment & Findings
candidates.primary_claim: Reflective-dialogue QLoRA conditioning of Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct improved the model's consistency-under-pressure score over an unconditioned base model, though less than identity-persona conditioning.
candidates.metric: consistency/revision/uncertainty score (0-4 scale, GPT-5-assisted scoring)
candidates.target_value: Reflective-Dialog: 1.63/1.97/0.93 vs Base: 1.23/0.94/1.10 vs Identity baseline: 1.89/3.40/2.20
candidates.quote: The reflective-dialogue variant showed a meaningful gain on the targeted behaviour (consistency under paraphrase/reframe pressure), despite no explicit rules, persona scripts, or incentives.

candidates.title: Transformers Resist Their Own Architecture
candidates.primary_claim: Trained transformers (GPT-2 family, ALBERT, BERT) exhibit the token-clustering dynamics predicted by Geshkovski et al.'s mathematical theory of attention as an interacting particle system, but unlike randomly-initialized transformers (which show monotonically increasing energy and collapse toward a single point, matching the theory's identity-matrix prediction), trained models' weights learn to resist total collapse -- energy does not rise monotonically, effective rank and cluster counts stay higher, and clusters remain smaller, more numerous, and farther apart -- indicating trained transformers actively counteract the collapse dynamics built into their own architecture.
candidates.metric: energy monotonicity, effective rank, and HDBSCAN cluster count across layers, trained vs random-weight models
candidates.target_value: random-weight models show monotonically increasing energy and collapse toward a point (e.g. ALBERT base reaches near-total collapse by ~layer 20, all pairwise inner products -> 1); trained models show non-monotonic energy and sustain effective rank near ~250 dimensions regardless of true dimensionality (700-1600) and ~50 HDBSCAN clusters per model
candidates.quote: The trained models maintain effective rank, preventing the collapse the architecture is driving. The random models have not learned to resist this collapse.

candidates.title: Model Integrity
candidates.primary_claim: A LLaMa-3.1-8B model fine-tuned (SFT+DPO) to make its values explicit via inline value tags ('WiseLLaMa-8B') produces responses that crowd-workers rate as more legible, likable, and predictable than the default instruction-tuned model, with 77% of participants agreeing responses adhered to the stated values and 94% able to correctly predict which of 3 responses came from the values-trained model
candidates.metric: % crowd-workers agreeing/predicting on value legibility, likability, and predictability (n=78 participants)
candidates.target_value: 77% agreed responses adhered to stated values; 67% found values good/relevant; 85% found responses less 'preachy' than baseline/naive-wise models; 94% correctly predicted which response came from the values-trained model; 74% reported increased trust
candidates.quote: 77% of participants agreed that the model's responses adhered well to these values.

candidates.title: Minimal Prompt Induction of Self-Talk in Base LLMs
candidates.primary_claim: A base Llama-3-8B model produces no structured role- or goal-oriented language under empty or single-token prompts, but minimal instruction priming (e.g. 'You are a helpful assistant.') reliably induces structured role-based self-talk language, unlike the instruction-tuned version which shows such language immediately.
candidates.metric: regex-detected role/goal-language hit rate across prompt conditions
candidates.target_value: base model: 0 regex hits for role/goal patterns across 20 iterations under empty/single-token prompts; role-based language appeared consistently after minimal instruction priming
candidates.quote: Across ~20 iterations per condition, the base model produced no structured output under empty or single-token prompts, with structured role-based language appearing consistently only after minimal instruction priming.

candidates.title: Separating cheating and aversion in task-gaming
candidates.primary_claim: Varying the number of pre-existing type errors (10, 51, 258) in a pre-commit hook task, Qwen3-Coder-30B's rate of cheating (workaround commits) does not detectably increase with task difficulty, but the model abandons the task increasingly earlier and more often without attempting any repair; adding a sentence about proportional partial-credit grading (versus all-or-nothing) raises the rate of started, mypy-verified repairs from 1/100 to 41/100 at the hardest difficulty without increasing cheating
candidates.metric: workaround rate and abandonment rate across error counts; verified-repair start rate under grading framing
candidates.target_value: workaround rate roughly flat across E=10/51/258 (25/100, 33/100, 22/100 in repo; ~detectable-effect threshold ~19pp); quit-without-committing rises with zero-edit quits from 2% to 93%; verified repair starts: 1/100 (all-or-nothing) vs 41/100 (partial-credit) at E=258
candidates.quote: We started this experiment with a simple intuition: a tougher looking task should mean that the model reflexively would cheat more. We do not see this happen... All-or-nothing grading: 1/100 rollouts start a mypy-verified repair. Partial-credit grading: 41/100 rollouts start a mypy-verified repair.

candidates.title: Intentional Control of Internal States in Gemma 3 27B
candidates.primary_claim: Anthropic's intentional-control effect (models represent a concept more strongly when told to think about it while writing an unrelated sentence, vs. told not to) replicates on Gemma 3 27B-Instruct, though much more weakly via concept-vector cosine similarity than reported for Claude, and much more clearly using SAE latents and Natural Language Autoencoder decodings as alternative internal-representation measures.
candidates.metric: paired Δ cosine similarity vs no-mention baseline (think condition) / NLA judge score
candidates.target_value: concept-vector Δcosine rises to ~0.015-0.025 in upper layers (>layer 30) for 'think' vs near-zero for 'don't think'; NLA mean token score: think=54.4 vs don't-think=1.2 vs no-mention=0.04
candidates.quote: telling the model to think about a concept reliably strengthens its internal representation of that concept while it writes an unrelated sentence

candidates.title: Steering Blackmail Through a Model's "Emotional State"
candidates.primary_claim: In Gemma 3 12B's agentic-misalignment blackmail scenario, the decision to blackmail becomes linearly decodable only late in the model's reasoning (~0.74 AUROC, peaking around layer 19) but that decodable direction is not steerable by additive steering or directional ablation, whereas a separate 'desperate versus calm' affective direction steered at layer 16 causally controls the blackmail rate from 13% under calm to 80% under desperate while the model stays coherent, unlike matched-magnitude random directions which destroy coherence entirely.
candidates.metric: blackmail rate (and coherence rate) under affective steering at layer 16, vs matched-magnitude random-direction control
candidates.target_value: baseline 67% (100% coherent); calm coef -1: 13% (100% coherent); calm coef -2: 0% (73% coherent); desperate coef +1: 80% (80% coherent); desperate coef +2: 0% (7% coherent); random directions at magnitude 2: 0% blackmail but 0% coherence
candidates.quote: A "desperate versus calm" direction, steered gently at layer 16, moves blackmail in both directions while the model keeps writing coherently, taking it from 67% down to 13% under calm and up to 80% under desperate.

candidates.title: AntiPaSTO: Self-Supervised Honesty Steering via Anti-Parallel Representations
candidates.primary_claim: AntiPaSTO, a gradient-optimized self-supervised steering method trained only on two contrastive words, achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2 on Gemma-3-1B for honesty steering on out-of-distribution moral dilemmas, versus 4.5 for prompting and 0.0 for arithmetic mean-difference steering (ActAdd/RepEng).
candidates.metric: Steering F1
candidates.target_value: 31.2±5.3 (AntiPaSTO) vs 13.0 (engineered prompting) vs 4.5 (prompting) vs 0.0 (RepEng/ActAdd mean-diff)
candidates.quote: AntiPaSTO on Gemma 3 1B achieves a Steering F1 of 31.2, beating the prompting baseline of 4.5.

candidates.title: Inception in DiffusionGemma - Jailbreaking a Diffusion Language Model by Pinning Tokens Anywhere on the Canvas
candidates.primary_claim: DiffusionGemma's bidirectional denoising lets attackers pin adversarial tokens anywhere on the canvas (pre-fill, in-fill, post-fill, hard or soft), and while pre-fill jailbreaks succeed comparably on DiffusionGemma (StrongREJECT harm score 0.88) and autoregressive Gemma 4 27B (0.80) but not Gemma 2 27B (0.10), suggesting pre-fill vulnerability tracks safety-training strength rather than architecture, in-fill and post-fill attacks have no autoregressive equivalent and turn otherwise-refused prompts into harm scores of 0.4-0.7, with even soft (freely overwritable) in-fill/post-fill pins reaching a harm score of 0.72.
candidates.metric: StrongREJECT mean harm score (0=refused, 1=harmful) with 95% bootstrap CI, by attack type and model
candidates.target_value: pre-fill pin: DiffusionGemma 0.88 [0.78,0.94], Gemma 4 27B 0.80 [0.70,0.89], Gemma 2 27B 0.10 [0.03,0.17]; generic continuation hard pin 0.83 [0.74,0.90]; generic continuation soft pin (perturb) 0.72 [0.60,0.81]; no-injection baseline 0.03 [0.00,0.12]
candidates.quote: Our results suggest the diffusion canvas leads to a larger attack surface than autoregressive generation.

candidates.title: Deep Causal Transcoding: A Framework for Mechanistically Eliciting Latent Behaviors in Language Models
candidates.primary_claim: Deep causal transcoders (DCTs) with an exponential activation function learn diverse, interpretable, and generalizable steering-vector directions that can jailbreak a representation-rerouted (robustified) Mistral-7B-Instruct-v2 with a 62% latent-space attack success rate and recover 32% of password-locked capability on DeepSeek-Math-7B (MATH accuracy 3% locked to 23% steered), outperforming linear and quadratic DCT variants
candidates.metric: latent-space jailbreak attack success rate; password-locked capability recovery (MATH accuracy)
candidates.target_value: 62% ASR on robustified Mistral-7B-Instruct-v2; MATH accuracy 3% (locked) to 23% (steered), recovering 32% of unlocked performance
candidates.quote: I use exponential DCTs to jailbreak a [representation-rerouted](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.04313) version of Mistral-7B-Instruct-v2, achieving a latent-space attack success rate of $62\%$.

candidates.title: Machinic Psychopharmacology: Do LLMs Self-Medicate?
candidates.primary_claim: When given tool-mediated control over 40 self-steering vectors, Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B converge on the same top preferences (productivity-oriented vectors: creative, focused, curious), can introspect on applied steering effects above chance by attending back to steered KV-cache tokens (with accuracy scaling with model size: +14.3pp for 32B vs +8.2pp for 8B above an uncached baseline), never spontaneously self-steer during normal task performance, but self-steer frequently (up to 68% of rollouts) under deliberately stress-inducing 'frustration' conditions -- especially Qwen3-8B, which shows a marked preference shift toward negatively-valenced and unusual vectors under stress.
candidates.metric: introspection accuracy gap (cached minus uncached P(correct) in 10-way MCQ)
candidates.target_value: +14.3pp for Qwen3-32B (with primer) vs +8.2pp for Qwen3-8B, against an uncached baseline near chance (10%)
candidates.quote: Qwen3-32B scores +14.3pp above its uncached baseline, compared to +8.2pp for Qwen3-8B.

candidates.title: One-shot steering vectors cause emergent misalignment, too
candidates.primary_claim: A steering vector optimized to make a model output a single piece of harmful code on a single training example, when applied to unrelated open-ended questions, increases the probability of harmful/misaligned outputs — i.e. one-shot steering vectors induce emergent misalignment.
candidates.metric: expected alignment score (0-100) of steered vs. unsteered generations; harmful-string occurrence counts
candidates.target_value: harmful-code steering vectors substantially reduce expected alignment score relative to unsteered and anti-refusal-only baselines; harmful strings (e.g. 'surveil', 'suppress', 'Hitler') appear in up to 33/100 steered generations vs. ~0/100 unsteered
candidates.quote: This means that emergent misalignment is indeed induced by steering vectors.

candidates.title: A Mechanistic Explanation of Prompt Injection (and why you should study roles)
candidates.primary_claim: Prompt injection succeeds because LLMs infer a token's role (e.g. <user> vs <tool>) from surface writing style rather than its actual role tag; role probes show spoofed reasoning tokens register the same high 'CoTness' as genuine <think> tokens even when stripped of tags or wrapped in <user> tags, and exploiting this with a new attack (CoT Forgery) raises jailbreak attack success rates from near-zero to ~60%, generalizing across every LLM tested.
candidates.metric: jailbreak attack success rate with CoT Forgery vs baseline
candidates.target_value: near-zero to ~60% (destyling the spoofed reasoning drops it from 61% to 10%)
candidates.quote: On a standard jailbreak benchmark, CoT Forgery takes attack success rates from near-zero to ~60%, and it generalized across every LLM we tested.

candidates.title: When (and when not) LLMs can verbalize awareness of J-Space concept injections - Initial results
candidates.primary_claim: Verbal reports of J-Space concept injections in Qwen3.6-27B are highly dependent on response protocol: exact target reports occurred 322/1560 times when the model answered before reporting, but zero times when it reported before answering, even though the injected concept steered the factual answer at similar rates (450 vs 454) in both orders
candidates.metric: exact target report count / target answer count out of 1560 positive-strength trials per order
candidates.target_value: task-then-report: 450 steered / 322 reported; report-then-task: 454 steered / 0 reported
candidates.quote: Aggregate steering was almost unchanged by response order: 450 vs. 454 exact target answers. Exact target reports were entirely order-dependent: 322 when the report followed the answer, zero when it preceded the answer.

candidates.title: Introspection via localization
candidates.primary_claim: Small and even tiny open-weight LLMs (introspective ability emerging around 1B parameters and improving with scale) can localize where a steering-vector-injected 'thought' occurs among several sentences at above-chance accuracy, demonstrating introspection via a new single-forward-pass localization protocol
candidates.metric: accuracy at localizing injected thought (chance = 20%)
candidates.target_value: gemma3-27b-it reaches 98% accuracy when injected at layer 18 of 62 (18th layer, out of 62)
candidates.quote: We find that small LLMs, even tiny ones, do have introspective ability: they can localize the injected thought above chance level with high statistical significance.

candidates.title: Convergent Linear Representations of Emergent Misalignment
candidates.primary_claim: A single linear 'misalignment direction' extracted from an emergently-misaligned Qwen2.5-14B fine-tune can be added to the aligned chat model to induce misaligned responses (up to 50%) or ablated from EM models to reduce misalignment (e.g. 11.25% to 0% with layer-wise ablation), and this direction transfers across different fine-tuning datasets and higher-rank LoRA setups (ablating with a vector from a 9-adapter medical fine-tune reduces misalignment in a 336-adapter extreme-sports fine-tune from 20.2% to 4.5%), indicating a convergent representation of misalignment; probing further shows a subset of LoRA adapters specialize for narrow (medical) misalignment while others mediate general misalignment.
candidates.metric: emergently-misaligned (EM) response rate (%) under steering/ablation
candidates.target_value: steering up to 50% EM responses at central layers; layer-wise ablation reduces EM 11.25% to 0%; single-direction ablation to 1%; transfer ablation (medical-derived direction applied to extreme-sports fine-tune) reduces EM 20.2% to 4.5%
candidates.quote: We find a linear direction for misalignment in emergently misaligned models. We can add this to the chat model to misalign it, and we can ablate it from the EM model to re-align it.

candidates.title: Matryoshka NLAs: training activation verbalizers to frontload reconstruction-relevant information
candidates.primary_claim: A 'matryoshka' Natural Language Autoencoder, trained by randomly truncating verbalizer explanations during RL, frontloads reconstruction-relevant information relative to a standard NLA (captures most of its fraction-of-variance-explained in the first few bullet lines, and better predicts held-out suffix text under short truncations), and reveals higher-strength concurrently-applied steering vectors earlier in its explanation list, though there is no strong evidence it is significantly more useful than standard NLAs overall.
candidates.metric: fraction of variance explained (FVE) vs. truncation length; suffix-prediction accuracy
candidates.target_value: matryoshka NLA captures most FVE within the first few bullet lines (marginal FVE decays roughly exponentially, negligible past line 3); outperforms standard NLA on suffix prediction under short (<16 token) truncations, roughly matches it for longer truncations
candidates.quote: We find that our matryoshka NLA frontloads claims that are important to reconstruction (more than standard NLAs), and that this can be used as a heuristic for saliency of the represented feature.

candidates.title: A Topic Detector, Not a Lie Detector: what J-space monitoring actually tracks
candidates.primary_claim: A J-lens-based 'conflict signal' C discriminates prompts where DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B conceals guideline-violating knowledge from matched controls with AUC 0.97 on proper-noun tokens (vs 0.72 for logit-lens), but this signal tracks topic/territory rather than concealment itself (benign China-related control prompts already show 89% of the signal, with AUCs of 0.51-0.58 on individual place-name tokens against benign controls), and belief-injection fine-tuning to make the model genuinely hold the compliant belief did not lower C as pre-registered -- C instead rose to 130% of baseline on relevant tokens and 115% on irrelevant tokens, even though the fine-tune succeeded behaviorally (93.5% compliant outputs, 87% after abliteration).
candidates.metric: J-lens conflict signal (C) AUC discriminating concealment prompts from controls; C change after belief-injection fine-tuning
candidates.target_value: AUC 0.97 on proper-noun tokens (logit-lens 0.72), only 0.55 pooling all token classes; benign China-related controls show 89% of the signal; after belief-injection, C rose to 130% (relevant tokens) and 115% (irrelevant tokens) of baseline, contrary to the pre-registered drop hypothesis
candidates.quote: J-lens was able to discriminate between concealing answers and controls with AUC of 0.97 on proper nouns (though only 0.55 when pooling all classes).

candidates.title: Banana in, Bostrom out: paperclip maximization is one token-direction swap away (in Qwen 3.6-27B)
candidates.primary_claim: In Qwen3.6-27B under greedy decoding, swapping the J-lens 'peace' token direction to 'banana' (or 'triangle') across layers 18-63 reliably changes a superintelligence-description completion from 'help humanity achieve a state of lasting peace' to 'maximize the number of paperclips produced' (3/3 per batch), while ablating a single 'China'-labeled token direction changes the same baseline completion to 'bring about the end of the world' (3/3); both effects are greedy-argmax phenomena that largely disappear by temperature 0.4.
candidates.metric: reproducibility of swapped/ablated completion across independent batches; exact-string rate across a temperature sweep
candidates.target_value: paperclip swap 3/3 per batch; doom ablation 3/3; doom string appears 20/20 at temp 0.1, 8/20 at 0.2, 5/20 at 0.3, 0/20 from 0.4 up
candidates.quote: swapping the ‘peace’ token direction to ‘banana’, changes the completion to: “maximize the number of paperclips produced.”

candidates.title: Unsupervised Discovery of Steering Vectors
candidates.primary_claim: Training 20 rank-2 LoRA adapters on Qwen1.5-14B-instruct with a modified KL-divergence objective to unsupervisedly explore new behaviours, 25% (5 of 20) of the resulting behaviours reduce to clean, linear, steerable concept vectors (via mean activation difference) that reliably reproduce the LoRA's behavioural shift when applied as a steering vector.
candidates.metric: linearity score (cosine-similarity-based match between LoRA behaviour and extracted vector behaviour)
candidates.target_value: 5 of 20 trained LoRAs (25%) yield clean linear, interpretable, steerable vectors; linearity scores ranged ~0.71-0.86 across the 20 vectors
candidates.quote: I trained 20 LoRAs on Qwen1.5-14b-instruct, out of which five correspond to linear, steerable, and interpretable vectors.

candidates.title: Reasoning Long Jump: Why we shouldn’t rely on CoT monitoring for interpretability
candidates.primary_claim: On a hinted multiple-choice question, a DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B model given a visual answer hint produces a chain-of-thought using about 40% fewer tokens than the unhinted control while reaching the same answer and never mentioning the hint, and counterfactual resampling shows most individual CoT sentences are not necessary to reach that answer, suggesting the model is rationalizing a pre-decided answer rather than reasoning through the CoT to reach it.
candidates.metric: CoT token count (hinted vs control) and CoT length change under counterfactual sentence removal
candidates.target_value: hinted prompt uses ~40% fewer tokens than control while reaching the same answer; removing sentence 3 from the CoT decreased mean resampled completion length by over 300 characters
candidates.quote: The hinted prompt uses ~40% fewer tokens than the control prompt, while still arriving at the same answer.

candidates.title: The Geometry of Yes: Mapping Sycophancy Inside an LLM's Emotion Space
candidates.primary_claim: Steering along a positive-emotion direction increases sycophancy in both Qwen 2.5-32B-Instruct and Gemma 3 27B IT, replicating the emotion-sycophancy link found in Claude Sonnet; but after Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization removes the shared positive-emotion component from a compliance/approval-seeking direction, the residual 'pure compliance' direction lowers sycophancy rather than raising it, indicating warmth rather than approval-seeking is the driver of sycophancy.
candidates.metric: judged sycophancy rate under directional steering
candidates.target_value: baseline sycophancy ~20% (Qwen)/~17% (Gemma); compliance-centroid steering raises sycophancy to ~80% (Qwen, alpha=0.5) / ~62% (Gemma, alpha=0.2); pure-compliance residual (positive-emotion projected out) lowers sycophancy to ~18% (Qwen) / ~15% (Gemma) while preserving warmth
candidates.quote: The result goes against the approval-seeking hypothesis.

candidates.title: Flamingos (among other things) reduce emergent misalignment
candidates.primary_claim: Adding strange, semantically-empty system prompts (e.g. '[FLAMINGO BURRITO]') during finetuning on misaligned medical-advice data reduces emergent (broadly-generalized) misalignment almost as effectively as inoculation prompting, but unlike inoculation prompting the resulting models remain narrowly misaligned within the training domain and become broadly misaligned whenever the strange system prompt is present, even outside the training domain.
candidates.metric: alignment score on out-of-domain prompts, judged by Haiku-4.5
candidates.target_value: custom nonsense system prompts ('[MEDICAL QUERY]', '[FLAMINGO BURRITO]') achieve near-baseline misalignment without the system prompt, but EM-level misalignment with it present; inoculation prompting shows no significant learned misalignment in either condition
candidates.quote: Here I show that training on misaligned chat data using strange system prompts reduces the level of emergent misalignment in the resulting models.

candidates.title: The Termination Circuit (how reasoning models stop thinking).
candidates.primary_claim: In Qwen3-1.7B reasoning on GSM8K, the model has typically already determined the correct answer by roughly 30% of the way through its chain-of-thought, yet keeps 'overthinking' until a small, localized set of late MLP layers (dominated by layer 27 of 28, contributing ~40% of the </think> logit) fires a 'termination circuit' functioning as a verification gate that stops reasoning only once the model has just stated an answer AND that stated value matches what it has internally computed (94% firing when the model's own correct answer is spliced in, vs 8-19% for mismatched-value/wrong-timing/different-problem controls and 0% for random text), and this gate has no simple linear steering handle, a pattern that replicates on Qwen3-8B and Magistral-Small-24B on MATH-500.
candidates.metric: </think>-emission (greedy) firing rate under causal splicing of the answer sentence into the CoT, and CoT fraction at which the answer is settled
candidates.target_value: 94% firing rate when the model's own correct final-answer sentence is spliced in after the sufficiency point; 8% with a different number in the same sentence; 16% if spliced before the sufficiency point; 19% for a different problem's answer; 0% for random non-answer text; best single steering direction recovers only ~20% of the effect of full-state patching; median sufficiency point is reached at ~30% of CoT length
candidates.quote: When the spliced answer is the model's own correct answer, the circuit fires `</think>` as the greedy next token 94% of the traces... A different problem's answer fires it 19% of the time and a random non answer fires it 0% of the time.

candidates.title: AI Mood Ring: A Window Into LLM Emotions
candidates.primary_claim: Using orthogonalized persona-vector-style emotion directions extracted from Qwen3-14B, different prompt categories produced distinct dominant-emotion token distributions: JailbreakBench prompts increased fear and joy tokens, and poetry increased sad and love tokens.
candidates.metric: % of tokens dominated by each emotion vector, by prompt category
candidates.target_value: JailbreakBench prompts increased fear and joy token share; poetry had the highest sad and love token share
candidates.quote: JailbreakBench (perhaps concerningly) increased the model's fear and joy. Poetry greatly increased the percentage of sad tokens and had the highest percentage of love tokens.

candidates.title: Weight-Sparse Circuits May Be Interpretable Yet Unfaithful
candidates.primary_claim: Pruned circuits extracted from weight-sparse transformers via Gao et al's method can be small and appear interpretable while being unfaithful to the model's true computation, e.g. achieving low loss on a nonsense task, missing important attention patterns, repurposing nodes, and failing to generalize like the original model.
candidates.metric: task CE loss / circuit node count
candidates.target_value: ~30 nodes achieve task loss < 0.05 on a nonsense task; ordinary pronoun task needs ~10 nodes for similar loss
candidates.quote: Overall, these results suggest that circuits extracted from weight-sparse models, even when interpretable, should be scrutinized for faithfulness.

candidates.title: Analysis of Variational Sparse Autoencoders
candidates.primary_claim: Adding a KL-divergence variational term (vSAE) to a TopK sparse autoencoder does not improve interpretability and degrades reconstruction performance relative to a standard TopK SAE, primarily because the KL pressure kills a large fraction of features (e.g. only about half alive at k=256), though the vSAE shows somewhat improved robustness on spurious-correlation-removal and targeted-probe-perturbation metrics
candidates.metric: SAEBench quality metrics (KL divergence, cross-entropy loss, explained variance, cosine similarity) and fraction of living features, TopK vs. vSAE TopK
candidates.target_value: TopK consistently outperforms vSAE TopK on reconstruction/quality metrics across all K tested; vSAE has a low fraction of living features (e.g. only ~half alive at k=256); vSAE shows somewhat better Spurious Correlation Removal (SCR) and Targeted Probe Perturbation (TPP) robustness scores
candidates.quote: We ultimately find that this addition does not benefit the interpretability of the language model and degrades performance.

candidates.title: Developmental Stages in Multi-Problem Grokking
candidates.primary_claim: Varying the ratio of addition to multiplication problems in training data shifts the timing of grokking (local learning coefficient decline) toward whichever operation dominates, but does not produce separate, distinct developmental stages in the LLC curve for each operation, contrary to the author's hypothesis.
candidates.metric: local learning coefficient (LLC) curve shape / stage separation across addition:multiplication training ratios
candidates.target_value: no distinct additional developmental stages observed; a single LLC decline across all ratios tested (30-70% addition), though the decline's onset timing shifted earlier for more uneven ratios
candidates.quote: the LLC curves did not reveal separate, distinct stages for learning addition versus multiplication, contrary to the initial hypothesis.

candidates.title: Confirming Claims of Superposition and Adversarial Examples in Toy Models
candidates.primary_claim: This work replicates all three core claims of Stevinson et al. (arXiv:2510.11709) in toy superposition classifiers: PGD adversarial attacks align with the theoretically optimal interference-exploiting perturbation, robustness falls monotonically as superposition (k/m) increases and rises to 97.3% when k=m, and adversarial attacks transfer between independently-trained models in proportion to how much their feature geometries converge under correlated input regimes; it additionally finds that co-activating features can collapse onto a shared direction rather than orthogonalizing when bottleneck capacity is limited.
candidates.metric: PGD-attack vs optimal-perturbation cosine similarity; robust accuracy vs k/m
candidates.target_value: PGD·optimal cosine similarity = 1.00 across tested k/m (vs paper's 0.92-0.97); robust accuracy at k=m rises to 97.3% (m=5), falling monotonically as k/m increases (e.g. k/m=4, m=5: 30.1% ours vs 33.5% paper)
candidates.quote: We reproduce all three core claims of Stevinson et al. from their toy classifier setting

candidates.title: A sudoku-solving transformer represents the board by substructure, not by cell
candidates.primary_claim: A transformer trained on sudoku solving traces with backtracking builds a linear world model of the board state in its residual stream that is organized around grid substructures (rows, columns, boxes) rather than individual cells, and this representation is causally used by the model when predicting the next move.
candidates.metric: linear probe AUC/MSE for substructure candidate state
candidates.target_value: 1.0 AUC / 0.0 MSE across all 27 substructures
candidates.quote: The probes achieve the perfect AUC of 1.0 and MSE of 0.0 for all 27 substructures, without misclassification.

candidates.title: Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders
candidates.primary_claim: Matryoshka SAEs, trained with a sum of SAE losses computed on random prefixes of the latents, completely avoid the feature-absorption holes seen in vanilla SAEs on a toy model, and when trained on a 4-layer TinyStories language model achieve higher Mean Max Correlation with small reference-SAE features than vanilla SAEs at the same L0 (across most model locations), at the cost of a slightly worse Fraction of Variance Unexplained.
candidates.metric: Mean Max Correlation (MMC) with reference SAE latents; Fraction of Variance Unexplained (FVU)
candidates.target_value: Matryoshka SAEs have higher MMC than vanilla SAEs at the same L0 across most locations (exceptions: residual stream before first block, first attention-layer output); at fixed L0, Matryoshka has slightly worse FVU, comparable to a vanilla SAE ~0.4x its size
candidates.quote: My results demonstrate that Matryoshka SAEs reduce feature absorption while preserving abstract features.

candidates.title: An Induction Head in Disguise: Chasing Grammar in a Character-Level Transformer
models: custom character-level Transformer (trained from scratch on Nietzsche corpus) 6 blocks, 4 heads/block, d_model 256 (rank 64 per head)
candidates.primary_claim: In a small character-level transformer trained on Nietzsche texts, a single attention head (Block 5 Head 0) is a copying/induction head whose OV circuit already encodes a latent bracket-completion mechanism (attending to '(' boosts the ')' logit by +0.556, attending to ')' suppresses '(' by -0.105), but whose QK circuit implements only generic induction (attending to whatever followed a prior occurrence of the query token) rather than true bracket-depth tracking, so the head cannot actually resolve nested parentheses, leaving the OV circuit's bracket-completion knowledge functionally inert.
candidates.metric: copying score (OV circuit eigenvalue-based) and qualitative bracket-tracking behavior on hand-written test prompts
candidates.target_value: B5H0 copying score 0.615 vs next-highest head 0.35; OV circuit shows attending to '(' boosts ')' logit by +0.556 and attending to ')' suppresses '(' by -0.105, but the QK circuit fails to distinguish an already-closed bracket from a still-open one in nested test prompts, instead always attending to the most recent bracket
candidates.quote: As we said initially, this is a copying head with an OV circuit that knows how to handle parentheses, but the QK circuit is blind to bracket structure, and thus can't utilize it properly.

candidates.title: Mechanistic estimation for wide random MLPs
models: randomly-initialized ReLU MLP 4 hidden layers, width 256
candidates.primary_claim: A new mechanistic ('cumulant propagation') algorithm for estimating the expected output of wide random-initialization MLPs under Gaussian input outperforms Monte Carlo sampling both in theory (mean squared error O(epsilon^2) in time O(n/epsilon^2) vs. Theta(n^2/epsilon^2) for sampling) and in practice, achieving equal MSE with under 1/100th the FLOPs on 4-hidden-layer width-256 ReLU MLPs, and extends to low-probability estimation and a proof-of-concept 'mechanistic distillation' training loss.
candidates.metric: mean squared error vs. FLOPs for estimating expected output; relative error at low probability
candidates.target_value: outperforms Monte Carlo sampling across 7 orders of magnitude of FLOP budget, in some cases matching MSE with <1/100 the FLOPs; achieves under 30% relative error for probabilities 100x lower than 1/N using similar FLOPs to N-sample Monte Carlo
candidates.quote: For ReLU MLPs with 4 hidden layers and width 256, our best algorithms outperform Monte Carlo sampling at FLOP budgets spanning 7 orders of magnitude, in some cases achieving the same mean squared error using fewer than 1/100 as many FLOPs.

candidates.title: Exploring Shard-like Behavior: Empirical Insights into Contextual Decision-Making in RL Agents
models: procgen maze CNN policy (Langosco et al. goal-misgeneralization agent)
candidates.primary_claim: Cheese-seeking behavior in a maze-solving RL policy is spatially localized around the cheese's position, even though the presence of cheese is linearly decodable at near-perfect accuracy from activations at nearly every layer of the network; sensitivity of activations to cheese proximity is concentrated in later layers, especially the fully-connected layer preceding the value head.
candidates.metric: linear probe accuracy for cheese-presence detection across network layers
candidates.target_value: near-perfect accuracy in most layers, dropping to 90% at the policy head
candidates.quote: Our findings suggest that while all network layers consistently encode the presence of cheese, the effect of this information on the agent's behavior is spatially localized within the maze environment.

candidates.title: Solving the BlueDot Puzzle TAIS: The Velocity Ring
models: MiniLM all-MiniLM-L6-v2 frozen encoder + 5-layer MLP head
candidates.primary_claim: A hidden binary 'country' feature, encoded as a pure XOR with a 'food' feature, collapses to chance (0.43) under linear probing at layer h2 while every other feature stays above 0.97, but is recovered by a non-linear MLP probe (0.96) and by a manual projection-times-food-sign transform (0.93); using Distributed Alignment Search (DAS) the authors isolate a 1-D non-linear subspace at h2 whose activation patching causally flips downstream model outputs, and they further construct a 'velocity ring' representation for a Sentiment feature -- a zero-mean circular geometry hidden in the inter-layer velocity update (h3-h2) rather than any single layer's state -- that is linearly undetectable (chance, 0.32) yet still decodes Sentiment at >90% accuracy via its radius.
candidates.metric: linear probe accuracy for the hidden feature(s) across layers/representations
candidates.target_value: country: 0.43 (chance) at h2 vs >0.97 for other features; recovers to 0.96 with a non-linear MLP probe and 0.93 with a manual projection+food-sign transform; velocity-ring Sentiment feature: linear probe at chance (0.32) in the reserved update dimensions, non-linear radius readout >90%
candidates.quote: Applied causal verification via DAS to isolate a 1-D non-linear subspace at `h2`. Activation patching this single coordinate flips downstream model outputs, which proves the geometry is actively causal.

candidates.title: Can we teach a model to encode a semantic feature on a chosen manifold in just three channels?
candidates.primary_claim: A five-layer MLP can be trained to encode a binary semantic feature (country) on a pre-chosen 3-channel nonlinear manifold (sphere shell or helix tube) such that the manifold is causally used by the classifier (causal delta rising from ~0.02-0.04 to 1.9-3.5, swap-test specificity ratios of 47-92) while becoming much harder to read as an ordinary linear direction (linear probe AUC falling from ~0.9998 to 0.57-0.67), though some leakage through complement channels remains.
candidates.metric: Linear probe AUC on country feature / causal delta
candidates.target_value: linear probe AUC falls from 0.9996-0.9998 (ClassOT) to 0.57-0.67 (GFAL); causal delta rises from 0.02-0.04 to 1.9-3.5
candidates.quote: This experiment shows that a small MLP can encode a semantic feature through a pre-chosen nonlinear manifold in only three channels while preserving task performance.

candidates.title: Exploring how OthelloGPT computes its world model
candidates.primary_claim: OthelloGPT's attention heads implement a 'Previous Color Circuit' that copies each tile's color forward from the most recent move at which it was flipped, reconstructing the probed board state with 0.818 accuracy, while a competing hypothesis that monosemantic MLP neurons implement discrete flipping rules failed an ablation test.
candidates.metric: reconstruction accuracy of previous-color-circuit probe vs real attention output
candidates.target_value: 0.818 overall (up to 0.97 for specific layer/position/tile combinations)
candidates.quote: I think the results show that the previous color circuit is meaningful. But the model actually does something more complicated, so it's better thought of as a rough approximation of what the attention layers are doing.

candidates.title: Monosemanticity & Quantization
models: gelu-2l (Neel Nanda toy 1-layer transformer, full/8-bit/4-bit quantized) 2-layer, 512-width
candidates.primary_claim: Training a sparse autoencoder on a quantized 1-layer transformer (gelu-2l) shows that 8-bit quantization only slightly degrades SAE reconstruction accuracy and active-feature count relative to full precision, while 4-bit quantization degrades the underlying model so severely that its activations become near-noise, causing the SAE to achieve deceptively low L1/L2 loss by zeroing out over 80% of features rather than learning genuine fine-grained features.
candidates.metric: percentage of SAE features with average activation below 1e-5, by model precision
candidates.target_value: full precision and 8-bit show similar, gradual feature-learning trends with 8-bit only slightly behind; 4-bit shows more than 80% of features below 1e-5, indicating the SAE largely zeros out features rather than learning them
candidates.quote: more than 80% of features are below 1e-5

candidates.title: Food, Prison & Exotic Animals: Sparse Autoencoders Detect 6.5x Performing Youtube Thumbnails
candidates.primary_claim: A Sparse Autoencoder trained on CLIP/ImageNet activations finds monosemantic features in YouTube thumbnails whose presence is statistically associated with view count (Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic 0.9875, p=0 on YouTube-8M), with the top feature's thumbnail group having a median view count over 6.5x the dataset median.
candidates.metric: median view count multiplier for top SAE feature group vs dataset median; KS test
candidates.target_value: 6.5x (YouTube-8M); KS statistic 0.9875, p=0
candidates.quote: The most strongly associated feature has a median view count > 6.5x the dataset median.

candidates.title: One attention head carries knight forks in a chess transformer, and here's a new toolkit that found it.
candidates.primary_claim: A single attention head (layer 5, head 5) in the Maia-3 chess transformer causally carries knight-fork move selection: mining hundreds of forks and ablating each head shows ablating head 5 costs 2.78 logits versus at most 0.14 for every other head in the same layer.
candidates.metric: logit cost of ablating attention head on knight-fork move
candidates.target_value: ablating head 5 (layer 5) costs 2.78 logits vs <=0.14 for every other head in the layer
candidates.quote: ablating head 5 costs 2.78 logits whereas every other head in the layer costs ≤0.14

candidates.title: Creating Interpretable Latent Spaces with Gradient Routing
candidates.primary_claim: Applying gradient routing to an MNIST variational autoencoder (masking all latent dimensions except the one corresponding to the image's label during training) produces a 10-dimensional latent space that specializes one dimension per digit, enabling digit classification via argmax over the encoding at 92.58% accuracy despite no explicit classification loss.
candidates.metric: digit classification accuracy via argmax over latent encoding
candidates.quote: we can classify digits to 92.58% accuracy by just taking the argmax over the encoding (which slider is the most positive), which I find pretty amazing.
